data.name: Counsellor
data.blurb: Int. The people class: spymasters, marshals, factors, gamesters, and the Hollowed.

traits.value: *Choose 3:* Deception, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, or Survival
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Finesse or Light property
*Choose 1:* Forgery Kit, Cartographer's Tools, Gaming Set (one of your choice), or Poisoner's Kit
*Choose A or B:* (A) Rapier, Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Crossbow Bolt Case, Dagger, Scholar's Pack, the tool you chose, and 2 GP; or (B) 110 GP.

rows.Class Features: Anticipate, Deduction, Mental Index, Read About It

features.name: Calculation
features.text:
**Defense.** You are where the blow isn't. While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Intelligence modifiers. If another feature gives you a way to calculate your Armor Class without armor, choose one. You can't add your Intelligence modifier to your Armor Class more than once.

**Strike.** You hit where the numbers say. When you make an attack roll with a Simple weapon, or with a Martial weapon that has the Finesse or Light property, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

features.name: Encyclopedic
features.text: You have read everything. You gain proficiency in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. If you already have proficiency in a skill you choose, choose another from the same list.

features.name: Observe
features.text:
You build a model of every fight from what you see in it. As a Bonus Action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The creature becomes **Observed** by you for 1 minute. You also learn one of the following facts about it of your choice: which of its ability scores is highest, which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus, one damage Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability it has (the DM chooses if it has several, and tells you if it has none), or whether it is Bloodied. You can Observe a creature that is already Observed, to learn another fact and start the minute again. Any number of creatures can be Observed by you at once. Wherever this class says "Observed," it means Observed by you.

You learn only what can be seen, heard, or measured. Observe never tells you what a creature thinks, feels, or intends.

features.name: Projections
features.text:
**Projections** are what you do with what you've Observed; each works only against a creature you have Observed. You can't use a Projection while you have the Incapacitated condition. The Computation Die column of the Counsellor Features table shows the size of your **computation die**: a d4 at level 1 and a d8 from level 5.

**Exploit.** When a creature you can see hits an Observed creature you can see with an attack roll, you can point out the weakness (no action required). You decide after the attack hits and before its damage is rolled. The attack deals extra damage shown in the Exploit column of the Counsellor Features table. These dice aren't rolled twice on a Critical Hit. The extra damage is the same type as the attack's damage; if the attack deals more than one type, you choose one of them. The attacker can be you, an ally, or any other creature. You can use Exploit once between the start of one of your turns and the start of your next, so not before your first turn in a combat.

**Direct.** Once per turn when you Observe a creature on your turn, you can also choose one ally within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. The next time before the start of your next turn that the ally makes an attack roll or an ability check against an Observed creature, it can roll your computation die and add the number rolled. The ally decides after seeing the d20 roll but before knowing whether it succeeds.

features.name: Sidestep
features.text: You saw it coming and were already moving. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down). You can use it a number of times equal to your Counsellor level (twice your Counsellor level once you reach level 3), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Anticipate
features.text: Anticipate is a Projection. When an Observed creature you can see makes an attack roll against you or a creature within 30 feet of you, you can take a Reaction after the roll but before the DM says whether it hits. Roll your computation die and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll. You can use it a number of times equal to your Counsellor level (twice your Counsellor level once you reach level 3), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Deduction
features.text:
You can go quiet and compute. You spend 10 minutes in stillness, doing nothing but thinking, and then ask the DM one question about a creature, an object, a place, or an event that you have Observed or seen, or whose evidence you have examined. The DM answers with the most likely truth that follows from what you have observed, in a sentence or two. If what you have observed isn't enough to support an answer, the DM tells you so, and the use isn't expended.

The answer is about what is and what is likely to happen: where the smuggler took the cargo, which of three doors is trapped, how many guards will be on the wall at midnight. It never tells you what a creature thinks or feels. If anything you based the answer on was false (a forged letter, a disguise, a lie you believed), the answer follows from the false data, and the DM doesn't tell you so.

Deduction isn't an ability check, and there's nothing to roll: an Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the clues, and Deduction is what you conclude from them. You can use Deduction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Mental Index
features.text: Choose two of your skill proficiencies. You have Expertise with those skills.

features.name: Read About It
features.text: You may never have done it, but you have read about it. When you make an ability check with a skill or a tool you aren't proficient in, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to the check; decide before you roll. The bonus replaces any other feature that adds part of your Proficiency Bonus to that check, such as Jack of All Trades. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Counsellor Discipline
features.text: You gain a Counsellor subclass of your choice: the Factor, the Gamester, the Hollowed, the Majordomo, the Marshal, or the Spymaster. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Counsellor levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Counsellor level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Counsellor levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Wider Gaze
features.text: You can Observe a creature within 120 feet of yourself, and when you do, you learn two facts about it instead of one.

features.name: Agile Nerves
features.text: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature while you have the Incapacitated condition.

features.name: Outdo
features.text: What you know, you know cold. When you make an ability check with a skill or tool in which you have Expertise, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

features.name: Total Recall
features.text: You forget nothing. You remember everything you have seen, heard, or read in the last year, word for word, and you can recall it at will. Your DM can ask you to keep your own notes at the table and treat them as your character's memory: what you wrote down, your character recalls word for word. Deduction now takes 1 minute instead of 10.

features.name: Cold Read
features.text:
When you roll Initiative, you can Observe one creature you can see (no action required).

**Your Read.** From now on, you read one creature at a time, and it takes the full weight of what you see. Whenever you Observe one or more creatures you can see, you can make one of them your **read**. It stays your read until you make another creature your read, it drops to 0 Hit Points, or it stops being Observed. Observing a creature you can't see (as a Spymaster can) doesn't change your read. Exploit adds its full dice when the attack hits your read, and half as many dice (round up) when it hits any other Observed creature. When you cast a spell (as an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction), Exploit adds half as many dice (round up) against every creature, your read included, until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Closed Mind
features.text: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have it, you instead gain proficiency in Constitution or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

features.name: Never Surprised
features.text: You have Advantage on Initiative rolls, and you can't have Disadvantage on them.

features.name: Far Projection
features.text: Deduction can answer a question about what is likely to happen up to a year from now, not only what is likely soon. The DM answers with the course events will most likely take if no one acts on what you learn.

features.name: Unreadable
features.text: Your mind is a closed room. Unless you allow it, magic can't read your thoughts or determine whether you are lying, and divination magic can't perceive you or learn your location (as with *Locate Creature* or *Scrying*). You also have Immunity to the Charmed condition.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Recovery is recommended.

features.name: Checkmate
features.text:
You see every piece at once. Your Intelligence score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22. In addition, when you roll Initiative, you Observe every creature you can see (no action required). You learn Observe's facts only about the one you make your read.

> **Playing a Counsellor**
>
> You don't have to be a genius to play one. The rules do the computing: Observe and Deduction are questions, and the DM answers them the way a trained mind would. Your job is to ask the right question at the right time. "What's it weakest against?" on turn one; "Where did the smuggler take the cargo?" after you've walked the docks.
>
> Say what you see. When you Observe, tell the table what you've learned, then say what it means: "It favors its left side. Hit it there." Exploit only works when someone hits, so the party needs to hear where to aim.
>
> Being right is the fun, and being right is also the friction. Direct is advice, and your allies can ignore it. Let them. A Counsellor who's right and gets overruled is a better scene than one who's obeyed. Deduction runs on what you observed: if someone has fed you a lie, you'll be confidently wrong, and you won't know it.
>
> If you play one of the Hollowed, make sure your table has talked about boundaries beforehand. A mind that computes without feeling is a hard fit for a party, and each table works out for itself how hard. Know the pitfalls going in, and keep the coldness in character.

features.name: Letters of Credit
features.text:
You are a factor of a house: a bank, a merchant company, or a guild, which you and the DM choose together. You gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill and with Calligrapher's Supplies; if you already have either, choose another skill or tool. In any settlement where your house has standing (the DM decides where; most towns and cities), you can deposit coin and valuables with it and draw them out again in any other settlement where it has standing, so your wealth travels as a letter instead of a wagon.

Some houses at work around 1668:

| House | Where | Known for |
|---|---|---|
| The Genoese bankers | Genoa, and the court at Madrid | Lending to the Spanish crown against its silver fleets (the *asentistas*) |
| The Bank of Amsterdam | Amsterdam (the *Wisselbank*, 1609) | The exchange bank of Europe's trade; its bank money was trusted further than coin |
| Stockholms Banco, and the Riksbank | Stockholm | Europe's first banknotes (1661); the bank failed, and the Estates founded the Riksbank in its place in 1668 |
| The goldsmith-bankers | London (Lombard Street) | Holding merchants' deposits and lending to Charles II |
| The court factors | The German courts | Supplying and financing princes and their armies (the *Hoffaktoren*) |
| The sarrafs | Istanbul and the Ottoman cities | Changing, lending, and remitting money for the court and its tax-farmers |
| The Armenian merchants of New Julfa | Isfahan, and from London to Manila | A trading network run on partnership contracts and letters |
| The Gujarati financiers | Surat, and the Indian Ocean | Moving money by the *hundi*, a bill of exchange honored from Mughal India to the Persian Gulf; Virji Vora of Surat lent to the East India Companies |
| The House of the Bird | Mutapa's court, Sofala, and the Cape | A royal treasury that learned credit from the Swahili and Gujarati merchants it hosts, and banks platinum's wealth as paper |

features.name: Assay
features.text: By handling an object for 1 minute, you learn what it's worth on the open market and whether it's counterfeit or debased. When you Observe a creature, you can learn one of the following instead of one of Observe's usual facts: the value of what it's carrying, whose coin it's spending (who pays it, or pays for it), or whether it's in debt and to whom.

features.name: Everyone Has a Price
features.text: As an Influence action, you make an offer to an Observed creature within 60 feet of you that can hear and understand you and is fighting for pay or plunder: a mercenary, a bandit, a hired guard, or any creature the DM judges is there for gain. It makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, it takes the deal: it stops fighting and leaves, or stands aside if it can't leave, and it does nothing against you or your allies for the next hour unless one of you harms it. While any of its allies are still fighting you, it repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns; on a success, the deal is off and it rejoins the fight, and you owe it nothing. You owe it its price, 25 GP times its Challenge Rating (minimum 10 GP), paid within a day; a creature you don't pay remembers. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus (maximum of three), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Underwrite
features.text: When you finish a Long Rest, you can underwrite one creature: yourself or an ally. You spend the house's money on it:. The first time before your next Long Rest that the underwritten creature drops to 0 Hit Points without dying outright, the policy pays: it regains Hit Points equal to a roll of your Exploit dice, as long as you don't have the Incapacitated condition (unless the underwritten creature is you). A policy that can't pay because you have that condition isn't spent: it pays the next time the creature drops to 0 Hit Points before your next Long Rest while you don't have it.

features.name: Debts
features.text: When a creature accepts coin, a loan, or a service worth at least 10 GP from you, it owes you a debt until it repays you in kind. Each creature can owe you a debt only once: once it has repaid or settled its debt, it can't owe you another. You have Advantage on Charisma checks to influence a creature that owes you a debt. You can call a creature's debt in once: the creature does one reasonable thing you ask of it that doesn't risk its life, and the debt is settled. The DM decides what's reasonable.

features.name: Follow the Money
features.text: You can spend 1 hour with an organization's accounts, or a day of inquiries among the merchants it deals with, to learn who funds it, its largest debts and debtors, and where its money is going next.

features.name: The House's Books
features.text: Your house keeps the books. In a settlement where your house has standing, you can spend 1 hour with its ledgers, or with its correspondents' letters, to learn what one creature or organization you can name has bought, sold, borrowed, lent, or been paid there in the last month, and through whom. Money that moves by letter of credit or bank draft can't move through your house unseen, whoever sends it: a bribe, a ransom, or a spymaster's coin.

features.name: The Market
features.text: Over a tenday spent in a settlement where your house has standing, you can move its credit against one person or organization there: its loans are called in, its suppliers raise their prices, its hirelings hear they won't be paid. The DM decides what follows, which can include lost holdings, deserting hirelings, or a rival who suddenly has the money to act. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a tenday of downtime.

features.name: Where the Action Is
features.text: In any settlement, you can find where the serious play is within an hour: where it's played, who keeps the bank, and who's welcome. You can learn any game of chance or skill by watching it for 10 minutes, and in downtime you can cover your own food and lodging from the tables without spending coin.

features.name: Honest Assessment
features.text: You can spend 10 minutes hearing a plan laid out, or 10 minutes watching its key people after you have Observed each of them (whoever leads it and whoever carries out its essential parts; the DM tells you who they are), and then ask the DM how it will go. The DM tells you whether it's likely, even, or unlikely to succeed, and the single biggest risk to it. When your assessment, given to a patron, proves right, you gain standing with that patron: you have Advantage on Charisma checks to influence it until an assessment you give it proves wrong. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Count
features.text: When a creature hits an Observed creature that is hostile to you and you could use Exploit, you can hold instead. At the start of each of your turns, if you held since the start of your previous turn and didn't use Exploit in that time, you gain 1 count. You can have a number of counts equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). When you use Exploit, you can spend all your counts: Exploit adds its dice once more for each count you spend. From level 11, if the hit isn't on your read (see Cold Read), count the dice first and then halve them. When you roll Initiative, your counts drop to 0.

features.name: Big Player
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you signal one ally within 60 feet of yourself who can see you. It can take a Reaction to move up to its Speed, and this movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from Observed creatures. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Know the Odds
features.text: When you Observe a creature, you also learn its Armor Class and its current Hit Points.

features.name: Everyone's a Mark
features.text: When you spend an evening at play with a creature, you learn how it bets: whether it bluffs, how much it can afford to lose, and its tell. For the next tenday, you have Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against it.

features.name: Stacked Deck
features.text: When you roll Initiative, your counts become 1 instead of 0.

features.name: Your Own Chair
features.text: Choose one gaming house, salon, or court where the high play is. You're a fixture there: you're always admitted, and you can sit down to play on your word. When you ask, its keeper tells you who has been losing, to whom, and how much. Anyone powerful who plays there can find you for a quiet word, and you can find them. If you choose a new chair, the old one forgets you after a tenday.

features.name: All In
features.text: When an ally you can see makes an attack roll against an Observed creature, and you have at least 2 counts and haven't used Exploit since the start of your latest turn, you can bet your counts before the roll (no action required). If the attack hits, it's a Critical Hit, but only the attack's own damage dice (the weapon's or the spell's, not extra dice from features such as Sneak Attack, smites, or *Hunter's Mark*) are rolled twice, and you use Exploit on it, spending your counts. If it misses, you lose your counts, and you can't use Exploit until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Debt of Honor
features.text: When a creature stakes something other than coin against you at play (a favor, a secret, a ship, a title) and loses, it pays, or everyone at that table knows it didn't. The DM decides what welshing costs it among its peers.

features.name: Poisoner
features.text: You gain proficiency with the Poisoner's Kit; if you already have it, choose another tool. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can make doses of your poison, using your Poisoner's Kit but no other materials, until you have a number of doses equal to half your Counsellor level (round up), to a maximum of your Proficiency Bonus; you can't have more than that at once. A dose lasts until you finish your next Long Rest, and only you can apply it. As a Bonus Action, you can coat a weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition with a dose; the coating lasts for 1 minute or until the first hit with the weapon or one of those pieces of ammunition, which spends the dose. A creature you hit with a coated weapon or ammunition makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, it has the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn. When you use Exploit on the hit that delivers a dose, the extra damage can be Poison damage.

features.name: The Quiet Trade
features.text: You can pass as an apothecary, a physician's assistant, or a household taster without a check, and you know the poison trade wherever you go: in a settlement, a day of inquiries tells you who sells poisons, what they charge, and who has been buying.

features.name: The Wound
features.text: When you use Exploit and the target can hear and understand you, the extra damage can be Psychic damage instead: you tell it what it can't bear to hear.

features.name: Blank Stare
features.text: Wisdom (Insight) checks to read you have Disadvantage, and you have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition. In addition, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for Charisma (Intimidation) checks, and a creature that is your prisoner, or that has the Restrained condition from you or your allies, has Disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks against you.

features.name: Mithridate
features.text: You have Resistance to Poison damage and Immunity to the Poisoned condition, and you can identify any poison by smell or taste without harm.

features.name: Vivisection
features.text: As an action, you can take an Observed creature apart out loud. Choose an Observed creature within 30 feet of you that can hear and understand you. It makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, it takes Psychic damage equal to the total of a number of computation dice equal to half your Proficiency Bonus (round up), and it can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Nothing happens on a successful save, but the use is still expended. This isn't magic. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Cause of Death
features.text: By examining a body for 10 minutes, you learn how the creature died and roughly when, and, if poison played a part, which poison and how it was given. You also learn whether a physician would have called the death natural.

features.name: Toxicology
features.text: Poison damage you deal ignores Resistance to Poison damage. A creature that has the Poisoned condition from your poison can't regain Hit Points.

features.name: Clinical
features.text: A creature that fails its saving throw against your Vivisection also has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn.

features.name: Taster
features.text: By handling food, drink, a letter, a glove, a ring, or a similar object for 1 minute, you know whether it's poisoned or trapped (a needle, a powder, a coated seal), and with what.

features.name: The Hollow Kill
features.text: When you use Exploit on your own attack against a Bloodied creature, roll each of Exploit's dice twice and use either roll.

features.name: Unmade
features.text: When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that saw it happen has Disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks against you for the next hour, and you have Advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks against it for the same hour.

features.name: About That
features.text:
You've already thought of that. When you're in a situation you could have prepared for, you can reveal a preparation you made earlier (no action required). You must have been able to make it: you were somewhere you could have made it, with the time and the money it took. Choose one:

- *Stashed.* An item from the Adventuring Gear table, a tool, or a weapon you're proficient with, worth no more than 25 GP times your Proficiency Bonus, is on you, or hidden within 100 feet if it's too big to carry unseen. You pay its price now.
- *Greased.* One creature that would take a bribe (a guard, a porter, a clerk; the DM decides who would) took yours. It looks away once, leaves one door unbarred, or carries one message, and does nothing else for you. You pay its price now; the DM sets it (a few GP for a guard or a servant, much more for an official).
- *Rigged.* A door, window, gate, or lock you could have reached earlier is unlocked, or a rope, a ladder, a horse, or a boat is waiting where you need it.

The DM can rule that a preparation couldn't have been made; if so, nothing happens and the use isn't expended. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Street Fighting
features.text:
You don't fight fair. When you use Exploit, you can roll one fewer of its dice to play one of the following tricks on the creature the attack hit:

- *Sand.* Sand in its eyes, a kick to the knee, its own cloak over its head. It has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.
- *Lift.* If the creature is within 5 feet of you, you take one object it's carrying that weighs no more than 1 pound and that it isn't holding (a purse, a key, a letter, a vial from its belt).

features.name: Crew
features.text:
In a settlement where you have found the underworld, you can hire a crew: a number of hands up to your Proficiency Bonus, at 2 GP a day each. A crew member will steal, carry, watch a door, follow someone, pick a pocket, run a message, start a brawl, or lie for you. It won't fight for you unless it's cornered, and it won't walk into danger it can see. When a crew member makes an ability check on a job you've set it, it adds your Proficiency Bonus plus 2 to the roll. A crew member who's caught keeps your name out of it, unless magic gets it out. Your crew stays with you until you leave the settlement or let them go.

*Who to hire, and who to play.* You know a settlement's gangs, crews, and factions, what each wants, and who hates whom. Once per tenday, with a few days and a little money, you can set two of them against each other (a rumor, a debt sold to the wrong person, a slight in the right ear): for the next tenday they're busy with each other and leave you alone. The DM decides what it costs and what it starts.

features.name: Racket
features.text: When an Observed creature you can see hits you or an ally with an attack roll, it owes you: the next time you use Exploit on a hit against it before the end of your next turn, Exploit adds one more die.

features.name: The Hum
features.text: Nothing moves through an underworld without you hearing of it. In a settlement where you have found the underworld, you can spend 1 hour and a few coins asking around, and then learn one of the following, if anyone in the underworld there knows it: who committed a crime in the settlement in the last month (a theft, a killing, a forgery, a smuggling run); where a stolen or smuggled thing went, and through whose hands; who in the settlement is paying for a crime to be done, and what they're paying; or what is coming into the settlement in the next tenday that isn't on the customs books. If the underworld doesn't know, you learn that, which is an answer of its own: whoever did it wasn't one of them.

features.name: Need to Know
features.text: You arrange the family's affairs so that each member knows only its part. When you brief a creature on a job (it must be willing, and the briefing takes 10 minutes), you decide exactly what it knows about the job, the family, and you. If magic reads its mind, compels it to tell the truth, or questions it after death, the magic learns only what you told it, and the first time that happens before your next Long Rest, you know it happened, wherever you are.

features.name: Fall Guy
features.text: Someone else always takes the fall. When you use Anticipate and the attack misses, you can make the blow land on someone else: one creature of your choice other than the attacker or the target, within the attacker's reach (or within 5 feet of the target, for a ranged attack), takes the attack's damage as if the attack had hit it. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Sit-Down
features.text:
Your name is known in every underworld, and bosses ask your advice. When you find a settlement's underworld, whoever runs it receives you as an equal, and over a tenday spent there you can put it to work: it carries out one job you set it (a theft, a smuggling run, a jailbreak, a forgery, a riot, a fire), and you pay what the DM says the job costs. The DM decides what follows. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a tenday of downtime. In addition, no jail or prison in a settlement where you have found the underworld holds you or your companions for more than 1d4 days, unless magic holds you there. You can also call a sit-down: the heads of two or more of a settlement's underworld organizations meet under your guarantee, and while they sit at your table, no one there starts a fight. You have Advantage on any check to make them agree to terms.

> **Playing a Majordomo**
>
> You're not playing a villain unless you want to. The underworld is an institution like any other in 1668: it's where you go when the law is the problem, and in a world of monopolies, sea bans, and witch-finders, the law often is. The Criminal background suits you, and so does any other; plenty of majordomos were born to a counting house or trained for the law, and found the books more interesting from the other side.
>
> About That is the fun of the heist without the hour of planning at the table. Don't plan everything out loud: get into trouble, then reveal that you'd already greased the guard. Your DM is the judge of whether you could have, so be generous with each other.
>
> In a fight, Observe whoever is hurting your people, and Exploit the hit that won't finish it off with a trick; save the full dice for the hit that will. From 14th, stand where the enemies are crowded together, and let them hit each other.
>
> Talk with your table about how much crime the game wants. A family's war, a heist campaign, a smuggling ship, or a party with one Counsellor who knows a man: all of them work. You're the one who says "it's not personal, it's business," and is mostly right.

features.name: Staff Officer
features.text: By watching a camp, a garrison, a fleet in harbor, or a column on the march for 10 minutes, you can estimate its numbers to within a tenth, how many days of food, water, and powder it carries, whether it has been paid lately, and whether it's getting ready to move. In any camp or garrison that isn't hostile to you, you can find a meal, a bed, fodder for your mounts, and the officer who signs things.

features.name: Battle Picture
features.text: When you roll Initiative, you and each ally within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you can roll your computation die and add the number rolled to the Initiative roll. In addition, you know the location of each Observed creature within 60 feet of you, even if it is Invisible or behind Total Cover, and an Observed creature can't hide from you.

features.name: Spotter
features.text: When you Observe a creature that isn't already Observed by you, the next attack roll made against it before the start of your next turn has Advantage.

features.name: Fire Control
features.text: You call targets as you see them. An ally within 60 feet of you who can hear you ignores Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover on attack rolls against Observed creatures, and doesn't have Disadvantage on attack rolls against an Observed creature for being unable to see it.

features.name: Lay of the Land
features.text: You can spend 10 minutes surveying the ground from a place where you can see it. The DM tells you the best approach to any one place within 1 mile, the most defensible ground in that area, and where an ambush is most likely to be laid on the way.

features.name: Logistics
features.text: Before a journey, you can spend 1 hour with maps, stores, and anyone who knows the road. For that journey, the party's food and water last half again as long, the DM tells you where along the route more can be had and what it will cost, and you know the day the party will run out.

features.name: Faster Than Thought
features.text: When you take a Bonus Action to Observe, you can Observe a second time as part of the same Bonus Action, choosing the same creature or another one.

features.name: Siegecraft
features.text: By studying a fortification, a walled town, or a fortified camp for 10 minutes from where you can see it, you learn its garrison's approximate strength, how long its stores will hold, its weakest point, and how a besieger would most likely take it. If you're inside the walls, you learn the same from the inside, and how long it can hold.

features.name: Called It
features.text: At the start of your turn, you can name an Observed creature you can see and call out loud the creature it will attack next. If the first attack roll the Observed creature makes before the start of your next turn targets the creature you called, it has Disadvantage on that roll; the warning came in time. If its first attack roll targets anyone else, the next attack roll made against it before the start of your next turn has Advantage; you read the opening it left.

features.name: Extraction
features.text: When an ally you can see within 60 feet of you who can hear you takes damage that would reduce it to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to shout the warning; it drops to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Terms
features.text: Commanders deal with you as one of their own. When you parley under a flag of truce or negotiate a surrender, a ransom, an exchange of prisoners, or passage through someone's land, you have Advantage on the Charisma checks you make, and you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for them. A commander who has met you across a field honors a truce you've agreed to, unless it has a very good reason not to.

features.name: Network
features.text:
You have someone, everywhere. When you are in a settlement, you can declare that you already have an asset inside any one place in it, however closed to you: a scullery maid in the palace, a fence in the thieves' den, a clerk in the guild hall, a novice in the temple. You can have one asset in each settlement. You have a number of **favors** equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended favors when you finish a Long Rest. You can spend a favor to ask an asset one question about the place where it works (who came through last night, which door the guards leave unlocked, what the abbot keeps in the strongbox). The DM answers as the asset would, which is usually, but not always, true. The asset won't fight, steal, or risk its life for you.

*Burned.* An asset stays yours until it is burned: exposed, gone, or turned by someone else. It is burned if you call on it in a way that exposes it, or by the heat: the first time you call on a settlement's network in a tenday, nothing more happens, but each time after that in the same tenday, the DM rolls a d6, and on a 1 the asset you called on is burned. You can't call on a burned asset again. After you finish a Long Rest, you can declare a new asset in that settlement, in the same place or another.

features.name: Human Behavior
features.text: When you Observe a creature that can speak, you can learn one of the following instead of one of Observe's usual facts: whom it answers to, what it values most, whether it is hiding something right now (not what), what it is most afraid of losing, or its price: what it would take to buy its cooperation for a day (some creatures have none, and the DM tells you so). This is an exception to Observe's rule against feelings: you read what a creature values and fears from how it lives (dress, posture, habit, the company it keeps), never from what it is thinking.

features.name: Dossiers
features.text:
You gain proficiency with the Disguise Kit and the Forgery Kit; if you already have either, choose another tool. You can Observe a creature you can hear but can't see, and you can spend 1 minute examining something a creature left behind (its handwriting, its tracks, the room it slept in) to Observe it without seeing it at all. A creature you have Observed this way stays Observed by you for 30 days, not 1 minute, but your Projections work against it only if you have also Observed it in the last minute.

*Disguise Kit.* You can use a Disguise Kit to make yourself up as a creature you have Observed, if it is roughly your size and shape. When you make a Charisma (Deception) check to pass as that creature, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the check. A creature that hasn't studied it closely and doesn't know it personally has Disadvantage on checks to see through you.

*Forgery Kit.* You can use a Forgery Kit to forge a document in the hand, voice, and seal of a creature you have Observed. You make the check with Intelligence instead of Dexterity, and with Advantage. A creature examining the forgery can make an Intelligence (Investigation) check to spot it, against a DC equal to the total of your check. It has Disadvantage on that check unless it has studied the creature you forged closely or knows it personally.

features.name: Profile
features.text: You learn what a creature can do before it does it. When you Observe a creature, you can learn one of the following instead of one of Observe's usual facts: its most dangerous attack or ability and whether it has used it yet; how many uses it has left of something it has used (Legendary Resistance included); whether it is giving the orders to the creatures with it; whether it has allies or reinforcements nearby that you can't see; or whether it is not what it seems (disguised, shapechanged, or under another creature's control).

features.name: Read the Room
features.text: When you enter a space where creatures are gathered (a hall, a camp, a tavern), you can Observe a number of creatures you can see equal to your Proficiency Bonus (no action required), learning Observe's facts about only one of them, your choice. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, a creature you have Observed in the last minute can't have Advantage on attack rolls against you.

features.name: Forewarned
features.text: When an Observed creature you can see uses an ability or casts a spell that forces a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to shout the warning. Each ally within 30 feet of you who can hear you has Advantage on its saving throw against it. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Without Portfolio
features.text: You answer to no one who can be named. When an official in a settlement where you have declared an asset orders you or an ally detained, searched, or arrested, orders your property seized, or bars your way, you can spend a favor to make that order go astray: the paperwork is lost, a superior countermands it, or someone else is taken in your place. The order can't be given again against you or that ally until the next dawn. This has no effect on anyone acting outside the law, and the settlement's ruler, or anyone who has studied you closely, can push the order through.

features.name: The Club
features.text: You can run your Network without leaving your chair. The Club keeps a few pairs of shewstones (Sending Stones, in the rules; *The Setting*, The World in 1668, Shewstones), the rarest of things, and you have the use of them. (The Club itself is in *The Setting*, The World in 1668, The Spymaster's Club.) When you spend a favor, you can call on an asset in any settlement where you have ever declared one, anywhere in the world: the message goes by shewstone to the Club's agent there, and the answer reaches you within 1 day.

multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following trait from the Core Counsellor Traits table: Hit Point Die. Gain the Counsellor's level 1 features, which are listed in the Counsellor Features table. Your computation die and Exploit's dice come only from your Counsellor levels. If you have more levels in another class than in this one, Sidestep and Anticipate each have a number of uses equal to your Counsellor level instead of the uses those features give, Exploit (still once between the start of one of your turns and the start of your next) is also limited to that many uses, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

data.name: Courtier
data.blurb: A new class. The accomplished person of every court's ideal, who makes it all look effortless.

traits.value: Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Finesse property
*Choose 1:* one type of Artisan's Tools, Calligrapher's Supplies, Disguise Kit, or a Gaming Set
*Choose A or B:* (A) Rapier, Dagger, Shortbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Fine Clothes, Diplomat's Pack, the tool you chose, and 10 GP; or (B) 120 GP.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. At Courtier level 9, you gain Expertise in two more.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.text: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose one accomplishment.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.text: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Rapiers and Shortbows. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

features.name: Courtier College
features.text: You gain a Courtier College of your choice: the art that finishes you. The College of Arms, the College of Art, the College of Grace, the College of Psyche, and the College of Verse are detailed after this class's description. You gain each of your college's features at the Courtier levels shown.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Courtier levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Coming and Going
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can choose to be noticed or to be overlooked, for 10 minutes or until you choose again.

- *Noticed.* Every creature that can see you and isn't hostile to you stops what it's doing to watch or listen to you for as long as you hold its attention, up to 1 minute. A creature with Truesight, or that is in combat, is unaffected.
- *Overlooked.* Creatures that can see you pay you no more attention than a servant, unless you attack, cast a spell, or speak to them. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to go unnoticed in a crowd.

You can do this a number of times equal to your Regard, and you regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of the Night Spirit is recommended.

subclasses.name: Psyche
subclasses.lead: * This college came over from the Bard. Music stays the Bard's, so Psyche works the passions themselves: Le Brun's lecture on the expression of the passions (1668) and Descartes's* Passions of the Soul *(1649). Its price: it forgoes Arts.*

features.name: Boundless Passion
features.text: When you Settle a creature, each other creature of your choice within 10 feet of it gains the same benefit. When a creature you've Stirred makes an attack roll against you before the start of your next turn, it takes Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Telling Cut die, whether it hits or misses.

subclasses.name: Verse
subclasses.lead: * Shakespeare's heirs, Molière, the commedia, kabuki, the ghazal, the pulpit orator, the filí's satire. Its price: it forgoes Arms.*

features.name: Satire
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to mock a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can hear you. It takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Telling Cut die plus your Charisma modifier, and it has Disadvantage on its next saving throw before the end of your next turn while everyone who heard you laughs.

features.name: All the World
features.text: Your work is known: any company of players anywhere in the world will stage a play of yours, and any court that keeps a stage will receive you as its author.

data.name: Mhizha
data.blurb: Int half caster. Mutapa’s artificer: magic through tools; I bring my laser into the fight.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Sleight of Hand
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Ammunition and Loading properties
Tinker's Tools, and one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice
Light and Medium armor and Shields
*Choose A or B:* (A) Scale Mail, Shield, Dagger, Tinker's Tools, the Artisan's Tools you chose, Dungeoneer's Pack, and 10 GP; or (B) 150 GP

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
You cast spells through the tools in your hands. See the rules on spellcasting for how spells work. The information below details how you use those rules with Mhizha spells, which appear in the Mhizha spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know two cantrips of your choice from the Mhizha spell list. *Mending* and *Prestidigitation* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Mhizha level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Mhizha spell list. When you reach Mhizha levels 10 and 14, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Mhizha spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Mhizha Features table.

**Spell Slots.** The Mhizha Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Mhizha spells. *Cure Wounds* and *Faerie Fire* are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Mhizha levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Mhizha Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Mhizha spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. If another Mhizha feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Mhizha spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Mhizha spells for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Mhizha spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You cast Mhizha spells through a tool: Tinker's Tools, Artisan's Tools you're proficient with, or your Arc Gun. You must be holding one of them to cast a Mhizha spell, even one with no Material component, and it serves as your Spellcasting Focus for that spell.

features.name: Arc Gun
features.text:
You carry a weapon of your own design that throws lightning. The Arc Gun is a magic item that only you can fire.

**Firing It.** The coil holds one charge and a shot spends all of it, so firing the Arc Gun is the whole of your Attack action: make a ranged attack roll using Intelligence against a creature or object within 120 feet of yourself, adding your Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the target takes Lightning damage equal to the dice shown in the Arc Gun column of the Mhizha Features table plus your Intelligence modifier. You can fire the Arc Gun only once per turn. This is a ranged attack, not a weapon or spell attack. You must hold the Arc Gun to fire it, and it takes one hand, so you can fire it with a Shield on your other arm; you can draw or stow it as part of the attack, as with a weapon.

**Rebuilding It.** If the Arc Gun is lost (out of your possession for 1 hour) or destroyed, you can build a new one with Tinker's Tools over the course of a Long Rest; the old one stops working.

features.name: Tinker
features.text:
With Tinker's Tools and 1 minute of work, you can mend a single break or tear in a nonmagical object you touch, as the *Mending* cantrip does, or build a Tiny clockwork trinket that does one simple thing (ticks, chimes at a set hour, walks in a line, plays a few bars of music). A trinket stops working after 8 hours. You can have a number of trinkets equal to your Proficiency Bonus at a time; if you build another, your oldest stops working.

*Retuning.* You can hear when a device has drifted. With Tinker's Tools and 10 minutes of work, you can retune a Mutapan curiosity (a self-lighting lamp, a stove, a pump, any small work that has fallen out of calibration) so it works as new. Anyone a Mhizha has taught can do the same in an hour; no one else can do it at all. Abroad, this pays: the owner of a drifting lamp is usually rich, often grateful, and sometimes talkative, and a retuning can get you through a door that a letter of introduction wouldn't.

features.name: Devices
features.text:
You build small devices that each do one thing well. You know two device designs of your choice from the Device Designs below. You learn more designs as you gain Mhizha levels, as shown in the Devices column of the Mhizha Features table. Whenever you gain a Mhizha level, you can replace one design you know with another for which you qualify.

**Building Devices.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with Tinker's Tools to build one device of each design you know. A device you built earlier from the same design stops working. You can use a device yourself or hand it to another creature; a device works for whoever wears or holds it.

**Magical and Electrical.** A device marked *Electrical* runs on stored current and isn't magic: anyone can use it, and an Antimagic Field or *Dispel Magic* doesn't stop it. Every other device is a magic item that doesn't require Attunement; it stops working in an Antimagic Field, and if you die.

**Durability and Loss.** A device is an object with AC 15 and 5 Hit Points; at 0 Hit Points it is destroyed. A device is lost if it has been out of your possession, and out of the possession of anyone you gave it to, for 1 hour.

#### Device Designs

**Arc Lamp** *(Electrical)*. The lamp sheds Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet, or in a 60-foot Cone and Dim Light for an additional 60 feet. It has no flame, works underwater, and can be shuttered or opened as a Bonus Action.

**Charged Plate** *(Electrical)*. The plate isn't armor, and it can be worn with armor. When the wearer finishes a Short or Long Rest, the wearer gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Mhizha level plus your Intelligence modifier.

**Clockwork Servant.** A Tiny clockwork figure that works as the servant created by the *Unseen Servant* spell, except that it's visible, it obeys a creature you designate when you build it, and it lasts until you build the device again.

**Lockbreaker** *(Electrical)*. A creature using it with Thieves' Tools adds your Intelligence modifier to checks to pick locks and disarm traps.

**Shock Gauntlet** *(Electrical)*. Once on each of its turns, when the wearer hits a creature with an Unarmed Strike or an attack with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d4 Lightning damage.

**Spring Boots.** The wearer's jump distances are tripled, and it takes no damage from a fall of 30 feet or less.

**Grapple Line** *(Electrical; Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. Once on each of its turns, as a Bonus Action, the holder can fire the line at a solid surface within 60 feet of itself and be pulled in a straight line to an unoccupied space next to that point. This movement doesn't cost the holder any Speed, and it provokes Opportunity Attacks as normal.

**Night Lenses** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. The wearer has Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

**Seeing Spectacles** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. The wearer sees creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition within 30 feet of itself as if they were visible, and has Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to discern an illusion.

**Breathing Helm** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 9)*. The wearer can breathe underwater and isn't affected by smoke or by gas that must be inhaled, and it sees clearly underwater. It doesn't let the wearer see through an area that is Heavily Obscured.

**Speaking Wires** *(Electrical; Prerequisite: Mhizha level 9)*. Two handsets joined by nothing anyone can see. Whoever holds one can speak in a whisper to whoever holds the other, if the two are within 1 mile of each other.

**Flight Pack** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 13)*. The wearer has a Fly Speed equal to its Speed. The wearer turns the pack on or off (no action required). The pack works for a total of 1 hour, in increments of 1 minute or more, and then not again until you build it again.

features.name: Preparations
features.text:
You make your own smoke, slick, and flash. When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 10 minutes of it with Tinker's Tools or Alchemist's Supplies to make a number of Preparations equal to half your Mhizha level (round up), to a maximum of your Proficiency Bonus. They last until you finish your next Long Rest, and only you know how to use them. Preparations aren't magical.

As a Bonus Action, you throw a Preparation at a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself, and choose which kind it is. Its saving throw uses your spell save DC.

- *Smoke.* A 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point is Heavily Obscured until the end of your next turn. A strong wind disperses it.
- *Slick.* A 10-foot square centered on that point is Difficult Terrain for 1 minute. A creature that enters it or starts its turn there makes a Dexterity saving throw; on a failed save, it has the Prone condition.
- *Flash.* Each creature in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

features.name: Mhizha Subclass
features.text: You gain a Mhizha subclass of your choice: the Chemist, the Constructor, the Gunner, the Lionskin, or the Mapmaker. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Mhizha levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Mhizha level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Mhizha levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Overcharge
features.text: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, you can expend a spell slot to overcharge the shot. The creature takes an extra 2d8 Lightning damage, plus 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

features.name: Field Workshop
features.text: You keep a workshop in your pack. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain expended Preparations equal to half your Proficiency Bonus (round up), and with Tinker's Tools you can rebuild one device that was lost or destroyed since your last Long Rest, unless you destroyed it or gave it up on purpose.

features.name: Flare
features.text: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against a creature other than you, you can take a Reaction to expend a Preparation and throw it as a Flash at the attacker before the roll. The attacker makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn, including against the triggering attack.

features.name: How It Works
features.text: You can spend 1 minute handling an object to learn what it does. If it's a magic item, you learn its properties as if you had cast *Identify* on it. If it's a mechanism, a lock, or a trap, you learn how it works, and you have Advantage on ability checks to operate, open, or disarm it.

features.name: Arc Chain
features.text: When you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, lightning leaps from it to a second creature you can see within 10 feet of it, which takes damage of the shot's type equal to your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Master Artisan
features.text: Choose two of your tool proficiencies. You have Expertise with them. In addition, crafting a magic item takes you two-thirds as long and costs two-thirds as much as normal.

features.name: Grounded
features.text: You have Resistance to Lightning and Thunder damage, and Advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: Lightning Itself
features.text: The Arc Gun's damage ignores Resistance, and a creature with Immunity to the shot's damage type has Resistance to it instead. Its damage rises to 5d10, as shown in the Arc Gun column of the Mhizha Features table.

features.name: Chemist Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Mhizha level specified in the Chemist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Mhizha Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Cure Wounds*, *Ray of Sickness* |
| 5 | *Acid Arrow*, *Lesser Restoration* |
| 9 | *Gaseous Form*, *Stinking Cloud* |
| 13 | *Blight*, *Vitriolic Sphere* |
| 17 | *Cloudkill*, *Greater Restoration* |

features.name: Tria Prima
features.text:
You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies; if you already have it, choose another type of Artisan's Tools. When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with Alchemist's Supplies to make three elixirs: one of Salt, one of Sulfur, and one of Mercury. An elixir is magical, and it lasts until you finish your next Long Rest. A creature can drink an elixir, or give it to a creature within 5 feet of itself, as a Bonus Action.

- *Salt* (the body). The drinker regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.
- *Sulfur* (the soul). For 1 minute, once on each of the drinker's turns when it hits a creature with an attack roll, that creature takes an extra 1d6 Fire damage.
- *Mercury* (the spirit). For 1 minute, the drinker's Speed increases by 10 feet, and Opportunity Attacks against it have Disadvantage.

*Assay.* With Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes of work, you learn what a sample of metal, ore, or coin is made of and how pure it is: whether gold is good, whether silver has been cut, and whether a bar has been weighted with a gray metal that isn't silver. Merchants, mints, and moneylenders pay well for this, and a House of the Bird assayer's word is accepted from Sofala to Surat.

features.name: Nigredo
features.text: You begin the Work by breaking matter down. When you fire the Arc Gun, you can have it deal Acid damage instead of Lightning damage; Arc Chain and Lightning Itself apply to the shot whatever its damage type. In addition, with Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes of work, you can dissolve a nonmagical object that fits in a 1-foot Cube and isn't being worn or carried (a lock, a hinge, a length of chain) into a black residue.

features.name: Albedo
features.text:
You purify what you have broken down. Your Salt elixir also ends the Poisoned condition and one disease on the drinker. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you can purify food and drink you touch as the *Purify Food and Drink* spell does (no action required).

*Green Salt (Level 6).* You know how to make the field dressing Mutapa's farms run on. During downtime, with Alchemist's Supplies, a week of work, and materials worth 50 GP, you can dress a farm's fields so that its next harvest is a good one, whatever else the season does short of drought, flood, or locusts. What that's worth to the farm's owner is for the DM; in a lean year, a great deal, and a village that's eaten through a famine on your dressing remembers you.

features.name: Citrinitas
features.text:
The Work wakes. Your Salt elixir restores 3d8 Hit Points plus your Intelligence modifier. In addition, when you make your elixirs, you can combine any two of them into a single draught, which grants both effects when it's drunk.

*A Drop on the Tongue (Level 10).* You can identify a potion, poison, or drug by tasting a drop of it over 1 minute. You learn what it is and what it does, and you suffer none of its effects from the taste.

features.name: Rubedo
features.text: You complete the Work. When you finish a Long Rest, you can also make the Stone, a red tincture that lasts until you finish your next Long Rest. A creature that drinks the Stone (a Bonus Action) is protected for 8 hours: the first time it would drop to 0 Hit Points without dying outright, it drops to 1 Hit Point instead, and the protection ends.

features.name: Constructor Spells
features.text:

features.name: Field Repairs
features.text:
When you finish a Short Rest, your construct regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum. If it had stopped working, it starts working again with those Hit Points; once you restart it this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

*Sentry (Level 6).* Your construct doesn't sleep. While you rest, it can keep watch; if it sees or hears a creature it doesn't know within 60 feet of itself, it wakes you with a chime only you can hear.

features.name: Improved Construct
features.text:
Your construct's Strike deals 2d8 Force damage plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Errand (Level 10).* You can send your construct on an errand to a place or person within 1 mile of you that you describe to it: to carry an object or a sealed message there, wait for an answer if you tell it to, and come back. It takes the route you'd take. It can't speak, and anyone who's met a Constructor knows to put the answer in writing.

features.name: Fail-Safe
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when your construct drops to 0 Hit Points, it drops to half its Hit Point maximum instead.

features.name: Turret
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you set down a turret in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself. It is a Small object with AC 15, Hit Points equal to twice your Mhizha level, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. It lasts for 1 hour, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, or until you set down another. You can set one down at no cost, and once more by expending one of your Hit Point Dice, and you regain both uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While your turret is deployed, it fires whenever you take the Attack action (no action required): make a ranged spell attack against a creature the turret can see within 60 feet of it. The turret doesn't fire while you're more than 120 feet away from it. On a hit, the target takes Force damage equal to 1d6 plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Rangefinder.* You know the distance to anything you can see, out to a mile, and the height of anything you can see the top and bottom of, to within a few feet. With 10 minutes and Tinker's Tools you can also tell whether ground is level, which way water will run on it, and whether a wall, bridge, or roof is sound.

features.name: Forward Observer
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can look through your turret until the start of your next turn, seeing and hearing what it would. While you do, you can't see or hear with your own eyes and ears, and you can fire the Arc Gun as if you were standing in the turret's space.

*Watch (Level 6).* When you set down your turret out of a fight, you can set it to watch instead of fire. While it watches, it doesn't attack and lasts for 8 hours instead of 1, but if a creature you didn't designate when you set it down comes within 60 feet of it, it sounds a chime that you hear if you're within 1 mile of it.

features.name: Shells
features.text:
When you would fire the Arc Gun, you can fire a shell instead. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 120 feet of yourself makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the Arc Gun's dice plus your Intelligence modifier; on a successful save, it takes half as much damage. You can fire two shells, and you regain both when you finish a Long Rest.

*Signal Shell (Level 10).* Out of a fight, you can fire a shell that does no damage and isn't expended: it bursts as a light and a sound seen and heard for miles, in a color and pattern you choose. Fired in a code you've agreed in advance, it carries a short message.

features.name: Bulwark
features.text:
While within 10 feet of your turret, you and your allies have a +2 bonus to Armor Class against ranged attack rolls.

*Siegecraft (Level 14).* With 1 hour to study a fortification, you learn its weakest point, roughly how long it would hold against an assault or a siege, and what it would take to make it hold longer. You have Advantage on any ability check to plan, build, or break a fortification.

features.name: Powered Suit
features.text:
If you have training with Medium armor, you gain Heavy armor training. With Tinker's Tools and 1 hour of work, you can make a suit of armor you wear into your suit. You can have only one suit at a time; if you make another, the old one is ordinary armor again. The suit's systems run down both arms, so it gives none of the following benefits while you hold a Shield. While you wear it, the following benefits apply:

- *Built In.* The Arc Gun is built into the suit; you fire it without holding it, and the suit is your Spellcasting Focus.
- *Gauntlets.* Your Unarmed Strikes deal Force damage equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier, and you use Intelligence for their attack rolls.
- *Tailored.* A suit is cut to pass. Out of a fight, it can look like ordinary clothes of your station: court dress, a merchant's coat, a laborer's wrap. A creature that looks closely can tell it's armor with a successful Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC.
- *Model.* When you finish a Long Rest, choose the suit's model. *Infiltrator:* the suit doesn't give you Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and your Speed increases by 10 feet. *Guardian:* when a creature you can see hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d10 plus your Intelligence modifier; you can do this a number of times equal to half your Mhizha level (round up), to a maximum of your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Kinetic Charge
features.text: The suit drinks the force that strikes it. When damage reduces your Hit Points while you wear it, or you reduce damage with the Guardian's Reaction, the suit becomes charged; it holds one charge at a time. The charge is the suit's whole store, and it goes out in one blow: when you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, or with an Unarmed Strike that is the first attack you make on a turn (you can't make another attack that turn after releasing it), while the suit is charged, you can release the charge. The creature takes an extra 2d6 Force damage (3d6 if the suit is an Infiltrator). The charge fades if you take off the suit or finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Suit Systems
features.text:
Kinetic Charge's extra Force damage increases by 1d6 (2d6 if the suit is an Infiltrator). In addition, you gain the following benefits:

- *Built-In Curiosity.* When you build devices, you can also build one Mutapan curiosity into the suit, and change it whenever you build devices again:. It works only for you while you wear the suit, and it's lost or destroyed only if the suit is.
- *Model Systems.* *Infiltrator:* you have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and when you fall, you take no damage and can move horizontally up to twice the distance you fall. *Guardian:* when you use the Guardian's Reaction to protect an ally within 5 feet of you, you can swap places with it, as long as you're both willing.

features.name: Improved Models
features.text:
*Infiltrator:* once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you have the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn. *Guardian:* you can't be moved against your will or given the Prone condition while you wear the suit, and your Reaction can protect an ally within 10 feet of you.

*Sealed Seams (Level 10).* While you wear the suit, you're comfortable in extreme heat and extreme cold, and you automatically succeed on saving throws against Exhaustion from them.

features.name: Flight
features.text: While you wear the suit, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

features.name: The Map
features.text:
You gain proficiency with Cartographer's Tools; if you already have it, choose another type of Artisan's Tools. You carry a map that draws itself: it shows any place you have spent 10 minutes in, you can't become lost except by magic, and it is your Spellcasting Focus.

*Fair Copy.* With Cartographer's Tools and 10 minutes of work, you can copy any map, chart, or plan you've seen, from memory, and you can tell at a glance whether a map is accurate, out of date, or a deliberate lie.

*Fold Space.* As a Bonus Action, you fold the map: a willing creature (it can be you) you can see within 30 feet of yourself teleports up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can do this twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Contour Lines
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you draw the ground steeper than it is. Each creature of your choice in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the Arc Gun's dice, has the Prone condition, and has a Speed of 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Survey
features.text:
You can spend 10 minutes mapping your surroundings. The map shows every secret door, hidden passage, and trap within 60 feet of you that isn't hidden by magic, and you learn the general nature of each trap.

*Route (Level 6).* When you plan a journey between two places on your map, you know how long it will take at each travel pace, the safest route and the fastest (rarely the same), and every danger the map has recorded on the way: a ford that floods, a pass that closes, a valley where cattle die.

features.name: Wide Fold
features.text:
When you use Fold Space, you can teleport two willing creatures instead of one, and each can teleport up to 30 feet.

*Longitude (Level 10).* You always know exactly where you are on the face of the world, latitude and longitude both, and the true time where you stand. A ship you navigate can't become lost except by magic.

features.name: Shortcut
features.text: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you fold the map along a line you've drawn: you and up to two willing creatures within 10 feet of you teleport to a place within 500 feet of you that is on your map. Each arrives in an unoccupied space of your choice there.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Mhizha Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and training with Light armor. Gain the Mhizha's level 1 features, which are listed in the Mhizha Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Mhizha levels (round up), as you would Paladin or Ranger levels. If you have more levels in another class than in this one, you know one device design instead of the number shown in the Devices column of the Mhizha Features table.

data.name: Natural Philosopher
data.blurb: Int. No magic: the laws the world already obeys.

traits.value: *Choose 3:* Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Survival
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Ammunition and Loading properties
*Choose 2:* Alchemist's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Glassblower's Tools, Navigator's Tools, or Tinker's Tools
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Crossbow Bolt Case, Dagger, Scholar's Pack, the two tools you chose, and 10 GP; or (B) 150 GP

features.name: Natural Philosophy
features.text:
You know the world by measuring it.

**Study.** As a Bonus Action, or over 1 minute outside combat, you study a creature, an object, or a feature of the environment that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. You can be studying one creature and one object or feature at a time; studying another replaces the earlier one of the same kind. A creature stays studied for 1 minute, and an object or feature until you finish a Short or Long Rest. This isn't the Study action, and it needs no check. When you study something, you learn one of the following of your choice:

- *A creature:* its Armor Class, which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus, one damage Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability it has (the DM chooses if it has several, and tells you if it has none), or whether it is Bloodied.
- *An object or a feature:* what it's made of, roughly how old it is, how it was made, or where it's weakest.

You learn only what can be seen, heard, or measured. Study never tells you what a creature thinks or feels.

**Measure.** You can judge, by eye and with the instruments you carry, the distance to anything you can see, its height, its weight, and its temperature, to within a tenth, and the time of day to within a few minutes.

features.name: Ballistics
features.text:
When you make an attack roll with a crossbow or a firearm, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. A firearm is a Pistol, a Musket, or a period firearm such as the pocket pistol (*The Setting*, Characters, Equipment and Firearms); the stonebow is a crossbow.

**Calculated Shot.** Once per turn, when you hit a creature you're studying with an attack roll using a crossbow or a firearm, the attack deals the extra damage shown in the Calculated Shot column of the Natural Philosopher Features table. The extra damage is the same type as the weapon's.

features.name: First Causes
features.text:
You can ask why. You spend 1 minute examining something in the physical world, and then ask the DM why it happened or is happening: why the bridge failed, why the well went bad, why the ward keeps flickering. The DM answers with the most likely cause that follows from what can be seen, measured, or tested, in a sentence or two. If what you can examine isn't enough, the DM tells you so, and the use isn't expended. The answer is never about what a creature thinks or feels.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Instruments
features.text: Choose two of your tool proficiencies, or one tool and the Investigation skill, gaining proficiency in Investigation first if you lack it. You have Expertise with them.

features.name: Mechanism
features.text:
You turn the place against the people in it, using a law of nature the place already obeys. You need a feature you're studying: a structure under load, a slope, a body of water held back, a fire or a store of powder, a pocket of gas or smoke, a strong light. It has to be part of the place: nothing you or your allies placed, lit, or created there. Most places worth fighting in have at least one: a chandelier or a beam overhead, a staircase or a slope, a canal or a cistern, a hearth or a powder store, a window in the sun. Expect one in most fights; the DM says so when a place truly has none.

As a Utilize action, you set off the feature you're studying with one precise act: a cut rope, a kicked wedge, an opened sluice, a tipped brazier, an angled lens. Choose a law from the Mechanism table that the feature allows; the DM confirms that it can do what you describe. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot Cube whose point of origin is within 60 feet of you makes a saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus); the Cube must be where the feature can reach, and the DM confirms where it can fall. On a failed save, a creature takes the damage shown in the Mechanism column of the Natural Philosopher Features table and suffers the law's effect.
