On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. The feature is then spent, though what it leaves behind stays; what's left (rubble, a flooded floor) isn't a new feature until the DM says the place has changed enough to hold one.

You can use this feature five times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

| Law | The feature | Save | Damage | On a failed save |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mechanics | A load, a slope, a hanging weight | Dexterity | Bludgeoning | Prone, and Restrained (pinned) until the end of its next turn. The area becomes Difficult Terrain (rubble). |
| Heat | A fire, a furnace, powder, a sealed vessel | Dexterity | Fire | Pushed 10 feet away from the feature, and has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn, scorched and dazzled. Flammable objects in the area catch fire. |
| Pneumatics | Gas, smoke, foul air | Constitution | Poison | Poisoned until the end of its next turn. The area is Heavily Obscured until the end of your next turn. |
| Hydrostatics | Water held back: a sluice, a cistern, a dam | Strength | Bludgeoning | Pushed 10 feet, Prone, and Restrained (mired) until the end of its next turn. The area becomes Difficult Terrain for 1 minute. |
| Optics | Strong light, and a lens, mirror, or glass that's part of the place | Constitution | Radiant | Blinded until the end of its next turn. |

A creature that has the Restrained condition from your Mechanism, or another creature within 5 feet of it, can take an action to make a Strength (Athletics) check against your Mechanism's save DC, ending the condition on a success.

Outside a fight, the same knowledge springs a trap from a safe distance, opens a sluice gate to flood a cellar, or brings down a wall where you want it to fall.

features.name: Aim
features.text: When you make an attack roll with a crossbow or a firearm against a creature you're studying, and you haven't moved or made another attack this turn, you can Aim before the attack: it has Advantage, and you can't move or make another attack for the rest of this turn.

features.name: Natural Philosopher Subclass
features.text: You gain a Natural Philosopher subclass of your choice: the Ballistician, the Crowner, the Experimentalist, the Naturalist, or the Navigator. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Natural Philosopher levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Natural Philosopher level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Natural Philosopher levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Out of the Line
features.text: You worked out the line of the blow before it was thrown. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

features.name: Leverage
features.text: Give me a lever long enough. When you Shove a creature, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the saving throw's DC. Once per turn, when you or an ally you can see pushes a creature, it moves 10 feet farther. With a lever, a rope, or a pulley, you can lift, drag, or brace as if you were two sizes larger.

features.name: Correspondence
features.text: You belong to the Republic of Letters. You can write to the learned world with one question about history, nature, a place, a creature, or an object. An answer arrives by letter in 1d6 days if anyone in your correspondence knows it, and the DM decides how much they know; if no one does, a letter says so. The answer is what the learned world knows, which can be wrong. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again for 7 days.

features.name: Conservation
features.text: Nothing a blow spends is lost. Once per turn, when your attack or a feature of this class reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, the damage beyond what it took to do so carries to another creature of your choice within 5 feet of it (no action required). The carried damage is the same type.

features.name: Experimentum Crucis
features.text: You design the experiment that settles it. You spend 1 hour testing a hypothesis about a creature, object, place, or phenomenon you have studied, and then ask the DM up to three questions that can be answered yes or no. The DM answers each truthfully. A question the DM can't answer from what the experiment could reveal gets "unclear," and still counts. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Explosion
features.text: You bring the reaction with you. As a Utilize action, you set off an explosion centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself; it needs no feature you're studying. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Mechanism's save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Fire damage of twice the Mechanism column's dice in the Natural Philosopher Features table (12d8 at level 15) and has the Prone condition. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried catch fire. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Eureka!
features.text: The answer arrives all at once. After 1 minute with a problem (a lock, a machine, a puzzle, a creature's weakness), you can ask the DM for the one thing you're missing, and the DM tells you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Skeptic
features.text: You've learned to doubt your own eyes. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition, and on checks and saving throws to discern or disbelieve an illusion.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: The System of the World
features.text: You see the whole of it. Studying a creature takes no action, once on each of your turns, and when you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended use of Mechanism.

features.name: Trajectory
features.text: Your attacks with crossbows and firearms ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover, and attacking at long range doesn't impose Disadvantage on them. In addition, from a hole, a wound, or a spent ball or bolt, you can work out where a shot came from, roughly how far away, and what kind of weapon fired it.

features.name: Gunnery
features.text: You are proficient with siege equipment such as ballistae, cannons, and mangonels; use your DM's rules for siege equipment (the 2024 core books have none; the 2014 *Dungeon Master's Guide*'s work, but they aren't in SRD 5.2.1; *The Setting*'s Arms and Armies covers what a siege is like in 1668). When you aim one, it uses your Intelligence modifier for its attack rolls, and its attacks ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover.

features.name: Master Gunner
features.text: You can judge a gun by looking it over: its caliber, the weight of shot and the charge of powder it takes, its range, and whether it has been overloaded, cracked, or badly cast and is likely to burst. Given 10 minutes to look at a wall, a gate, or an earthwork, you know roughly how long it would stand against the guns you can see or name, and where a battery would have to stand to breach it. Garrisons, armies, merchant ships, and foundries everywhere want master gunners: wherever there are guns, you can find paid work as one, at a wage the DM sets, and people who work with guns treat you as one of them.

features.name: Disabling Shot
features.text: When you hit a creature you're studying with an attack using a crossbow or a firearm, you can place the shot instead of taking your Calculated Shot's extra damage. Choose one: the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn; its Speed is 0 until the start of your next turn; or it drops one object it's holding. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fireworks
features.text: Given a day, your tools, and black powder and salts worth 25 GP, you can make a fireworks display that lasts about 10 minutes and can be seen for miles on a clear night: rockets, wheels, fountains, colored fire. A display at a feast, a wedding, or a ruler's birthday gets you noticed by whoever paid for the feast. You can also make up to six signal rockets as part of the same work; each, fired as a Utilize action, bursts in a color and pattern you chose when you made it, so that anyone who knows your code can read it.

features.name: Through and Through
features.text: When you score a Critical Hit with a crossbow or a firearm, the shot can pass through: one creature within 5 feet directly behind the target, in a line from you, takes damage equal to a roll of the weapon's damage dice (not doubled), of the weapon's type, without your Calculated Shot.

features.name: The Perfect Parabola
features.text: Your attacks with crossbows and firearms against a creature you're studying score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

features.name: Reconstruction
features.text: You gain Expertise in the Investigation skill, gaining proficiency in it first if you lack it; if you already have Expertise in it, you gain Expertise in another skill you're proficient in. In addition, you can spend 10 minutes studying a place where something happened in the last 24 hours. The DM tells you what happened there in broad strokes: how many creatures took part, what they did, roughly when, and which way they left.

features.name: The View
features.text: Given 10 minutes with a body, you learn how long it has been dead (to within an hour if it died in the last day, and to within a few days after that), what killed it, whether it was moved after death, whether it was alive when it went into the water or the fire, and what made the wounds: the kind of blade, shot, or blow, and from which side. You learn nothing about who did it, beyond what the wounds alone can say.

features.name: Find the Flaw
features.text: When you study a creature, you can also find its flaw. Choose one of the following, which lasts until the start of your next turn: its Armor Class decreases by 1, or it loses one Resistance of your choice (you learn which Resistances it has). Finding the flaw again doesn't stack.

features.name: What It Is
features.text: You can spend 1 minute studying an object to learn what it is: whether it is cursed and what the curse does, a magic item's properties and how to use them, or what poison or potion it holds. In addition, when you study a creature or object that is an illusion, you learn that it is one, and when you study a creature, you also learn whether it is disguised, shapechanged, or under another creature's control.

features.name: Standing
features.text: When you lay your findings about a death or a crime before anyone with the power to act on them (a county bench, a magistrate, a kadi's court, a village's elders, a ship's captain), they take you seriously: they hear you out, and they don't dismiss what you show them without a reason, though they may still decide against you. If you hold the office of coroner in England, or its like elsewhere, you also have the office's rights: to view any body in your jurisdiction before it is buried, to summon a jury and witnesses, and to commit the accused for trial.

features.name: Nothing Is Immune
features.text: The extra damage from your Calculated Shot ignores Resistance, and a creature with Immunity to that damage type has Resistance to it instead.

features.name: Inquest
features.text: When a creature tells you about an event you have used Reconstruction on, you know whether its account contradicts the evidence, and which part. You learn nothing about why; an honest witness can be wrong, and a liar can tell the truth.

features.name: Case Closed
features.text: When you roll Initiative, you can start studying one creature you can see if, since your last Long Rest, you have used Reconstruction on a scene it took part in or What It Is on an object it made or carried. In addition, when a creature you're studying uses Legendary Resistance, you can take a Reaction to expose the flaw. The creature must expend one additional use of Legendary Resistance; if it can't, it fails the saving throw instead. Once you use this Reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Apparatus
features.text: You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies and Glassblower's Tools; if you already have either, choose another tool from the Natural Philosopher's tool list.

features.name: Experiments
features.text:
When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with your Alchemist's Supplies and Glassblower's Tools to prepare two experiments: charged globes, sealed vessels, primed jars. As you prepare each one, choose one of the five energies in the table below: Fire, Lightning, Thunder, Cold, or Acid. An experiment lasts until you finish your next Long Rest, and it works only in your hands. You can't prepare experiments without your tools.

As a Utilize action, you release an experiment at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself; it needs no feature you're studying. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot Cube whose point of origin is that point (for Lightning, a Line 60 feet long and 5 feet wide from you) makes a saving throw against your Mechanism's save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes the damage shown in the Experiments table and suffers the effect shown in the table below. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

| Natural Philosopher Level | Experiments |
|---|---|
| 3 | 2d8 |
| 5 | 3d8 |
| 7 | 4d8 |
| 13 | 5d8 |
| 17 | 6d8 |

| Energy | Save | Damage | On a failed save |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fire | Dexterity | Fire | Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried catch fire. |
| Lightning | Dexterity | Lightning | It can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. A creature wearing metal armor has Disadvantage on the save. |
| Thunder | Constitution | Thunder | Pushed 10 feet away from the Cube's point of origin, and Deafened until the end of its next turn. The blast can be heard 300 feet away. |
| Cold | Constitution | Cold | Its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn. |
| Acid | Dexterity | Acid | Its Armor Class decreases by 1 until it finishes a Long Rest: armor, shell, or hide eaten away. This doesn't stack. |

features.name: Volatile
features.text: When you release an experiment, roll a d6. On a 1, it goes off badly: it still works, and you also take half the damage rolled (no saving throw).

features.name: Demonstration
features.text: Given 1 hour to set up and an audience, you can stage a demonstration: sparks drawn from a rubbed globe, a bell falling silent in a jar emptied of air, water frozen solid on a summer afternoon, a color that blooms when two clear liquids meet. It's harmless and it isn't magic, and anyone who watches it knows both. For the next 24 hours, you have Advantage on Charisma checks to impress, persuade, or raise money from anyone who watched it to the end.

features.name: Overload
features.text: When you release an experiment, you can overload it: it deals two more dice of damage, and Volatile goes off badly on a 1 or 2.

features.name: Touchstone
features.text: With your Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes, you can tell what a metal, an alloy, a salt, or an acid is, and how pure it is: whether a coin is clipped or debased, whether gold has been adulterated and with what, and whether a powder is what its seller says it is. You can tell platina from silver, which almost no one outside Mutapa can yet do reliably, and you know what that knowledge is worth to the people who'd pay for it.

features.name: Insulation
features.text: You have Resistance to the damage of your own experiments.

features.name: Freezing Mixture
features.text: With your Alchemist's Supplies, a supply of saltpeter, and 10 minutes, you can chill water, wine, or a room well below a cellar's cool, and given snow or ice to start from, you can freeze water solid. Kept cold this way, food or remains don't spoil for 1 week, as long as you renew the mixture each day.

features.name: Chain Reaction
features.text: When you release an experiment, you can release a second one as part of the same action, at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Roll Volatile for each.

features.name: Natural History
features.text: You gain Expertise in the Nature or Medicine skill, gaining proficiency in it first if you lack it, and you gain proficiency with the Herbalism Kit (if you already have it, choose another tool). When you study a creature, you also learn its habitat, what it eats, and one thing it does or fears; the DM chooses something true and useful. From a track, a nest, spoor, or a carcass, you can tell what made it and roughly when.

features.name: Bread or Poison
features.text: You can spend 1 minute examining a plant, a fungus, a fruit, meat, or water to learn whether it's safe to eat or drink and, if it isn't, what it would do to whoever did. You also know how to find food and clean water in a land whose plants and animals you have studied for at least a day, and you know which of its people's foods you've never seen are worth asking about. This catches food of the Hidden Realm too: measurement doesn't care what made a thing.

features.name: Know Its Nature
features.text: A creature you're studying has Disadvantage on its saving throw against your Mechanism.

features.name: Specimen
features.text: When you finish a Short or Long Rest after a creature you have studied has died, you can spend 1 hour with its remains and your Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies to prepare a remedy. As a Bonus Action, a creature can drink the remedy or give it to another creature within 5 feet. A creature that drinks it ends one poison or disease that kind of creature caused, or for 8 hours has Resistance to that kind of creature's Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against its poisons and diseases. You can have one remedy at a time; it spoils when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Cabinet
features.text: You can preserve the remains of a creature you have studied (a skin, a skeleton, a pressed plant, something in a jar of spirits) with 1 hour of work and your Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies, and it keeps indefinitely. You can tell a real specimen from a fake one at a glance, and you know roughly what a collector would pay for one; a well-made specimen of a creature no one has described can be worth a great deal, at a price the DM sets, and earns you a name in the learned world.

features.name: Field Survey
features.text: You can spend 1 hour watching and walking an area to learn what lives within 1 mile of you: each kind of creature, roughly how many, where they den, and which of them are hunting.

features.name: Know What It Does
features.text: When a creature you're studying forces you or an ally within 30 feet of you to make a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to give the saving throw Advantage. You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Plotted Course
features.text: You gain proficiency with Navigator's Tools; if you already have it, choose another tool. You and your companions can't become lost except by magic, you always know which way is north, and your group can travel at a fast pace without the usual Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception or Survival) checks. This works on every plane, not only the one you were born on.

features.name: Taking the Fix
features.text: With your Navigator's Tools and a clear sky, you can spend 10 minutes to fix your latitude to within a few miles, and the local time to within a minute; on land, with a telescope and a clear night, you can fix your longitude too. Given an hour and a day's travel, you can draw a chart of the way you came that someone else can follow, and you can read anyone's chart, whatever its language or its conventions, and tell how far to trust it.

features.name: Course Correction
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can call out a path. A number of allies up to your Proficiency Bonus who are within 30 feet of yourself and can see or hear you can each take a Reaction to move up to half their Speed. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your Natural Philosopher level (round up), to a maximum of your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Reading the Currents
features.text: When a creature you can see hits an ally within 30 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against that ally (round down). You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to half your Natural Philosopher level (round up), to a maximum of your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Safe Passage
features.text: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes a Dexterity saving throw against an effect you can see, you can take a Reaction to add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the save.

features.name: Drift
features.text: Your Speed increases by 10 feet, and Difficult Terrain costs you no extra movement.

features.name: Weather Eye
features.text: You can predict the weather where you are for the next 24 hours, and when a storm, a fog, or a change of wind is coming within that time. Near the sea, you also know the times of the tides, and on a monsoon coast, whether the season is about to turn.

features.name: Through the Gap
features.text: When you use Course Correction, you can also move up to your Speed, and you and each ally who moves can move through the spaces of hostile creatures. A creature can't end its move in another creature's space.

features.name: Pilot
features.text: You can bring a ship safely into any harbor or through any strait you can see, even one you've never entered, given an hour to watch the water first. Ships' masters everywhere need pilots: on any ship bound your way, you can work your passage as navigator or pilot, and the master gives you and up to five companions passage and food for the voyage in return.

features.name: The Path of Least Action
features.text: Overland travel with you takes half as long. In addition, when a creature you can see hits an ally within 30 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to have the ally move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; if the ally ends this move out of the attacker's reach (for a melee attack) or out of its line of sight (for a ranged attack), the attack misses instead. Once you use this Reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency with one tool of your choice from the Natural Philosopher's tool list, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Natural Philosopher Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with one tool of your choice from the Natural Philosopher's tool list, and training with Light armor. Gain the Natural Philosopher's level 1 features, which are listed in the Natural Philosopher Features table. If you have levels in another class, you can use Mechanism a number of times equal to your Natural Philosopher level (maximum of five), instead of five times.

data.name: Physician
data.blurb: Int full caster. The arcane healer.

traits.value: Medicine, plus *choose 2:* Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Persuasion, or Sleight of Hand
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, Light Crossbow and 20 Bolts, Dagger, Healer's Kit, Spellbook, Arcane Focus (crystal), Scholar's Pack, and 7 GP; or (B) 100 GP

rows.Class Features: Spellcasting, Physician's Eye, Healing Prowess, Diagnosis

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
See the *Player's Handbook* for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Physician spells, which appear in the Physician spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know three Physician cantrips of your choice. Whenever you gain a Physician level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Physician cantrip of your choice. When you reach Physician levels 4 and 10, you learn another Physician cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Physician Features table.

**Spellbook.** Your spellbook is a casebook as much as a grimoire: the spells you have learned, and the notes on what they did. It contains six level 1 Physician spells of your choice to start. If you also have Wizard levels, your Physician and Wizard spells can share one spellbook; each class prepares only its own spells.

**Spell Slots.** The Physician Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose a number of spells from your spellbook equal to the number in the Prepared Spells column of the Physician Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Physician feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Physician spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Physician spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells.

**Ritual Adept.** You can cast any Physician spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

**Undead.** If one of your Physician spells would make a creature it kills rise as Undead (as *Finger of Death* does), it doesn't rise; its body is destroyed instead.

**Expanding Your Spellbook.** Each time you gain a Physician level after 1, you can add two Physician spells of your choice to your spellbook for free. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. On your adventures, you might find other spells that you can add to your spellbook (see the "Your Spellbook" sidebar).

> **Your Spellbook**
>
> The spells you add as you gain levels represent your own research. You can also find spells on your adventures: on a scroll, in another caster's spellbook, or in a temple's records. **You can copy any spell that appears on the Physician spell list into your spellbook, whichever class the scroll or book was written for.** Copying a spell into your book takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP for each level of the spell. Copying a spell out of your book into another takes 1 hour and costs 10 GP per spell level.

features.name: Physician's Eye
features.text: You use Intelligence instead of Wisdom when you make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

features.name: Healing Prowess
features.text:
Your training lets you mend the body without a spell. You have a number of **Prowess Dice** equal to the Proficiency Bonus shown for your Physician level in the Physician Features table. A Prowess Die is a d6. It becomes a d8 at Physician level 5, a d10 at level 11, and a d12 at level 17.

As a Bonus Action, you can touch yourself or another creature and expend one Prowess Die. That creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

You regain all expended Prowess Dice when you finish a Long Rest, and one expended Prowess Die when you finish a Short Rest. From Physician level 5, Steady Hands sets how many a Short Rest returns, by your character level (see the table).

| Physician Level | Prowess Die | Regained on a Short Rest (by character level) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | d6 | 1 |
| 5–10 | d8 | All |
| 11–16 | d10 | Half your maximum (round up) |
| 17–20 | d12 | 1 |

> **Why the Return Tapers**
>
> The Short Rest return peaks in the middle levels, when Prowess Dice carry most of a Physician's healing, and tapers once the die is large and higher-level spells take over the work.

features.name: Diagnosis
features.text:
You learn to read a body at a glance. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself.

If the creature is willing, or is an ally that can't refuse (it has the Incapacitated condition or 0 Hit Points), you diagnose it automatically. You learn its current Hit Points and Hit Point maximum, every condition affecting it, whether it is diseased, has the Poisoned condition, or is under a curse, and the ability in which it has the lowest saving throw bonus.

Otherwise, make an Intelligence (Medicine) check. The DC equals 10 plus half the creature's Challenge Rating (round down), or 10 plus half its level if it has no Challenge Rating. On a success, you learn the following:

- Whether the creature is **unharmed**, **injured** (below its Hit Point maximum), **Bloodied** (at or below half its Hit Point maximum), or **near death** (at or below a quarter).
- Every condition affecting it, and whether it is diseased, has the Poisoned condition, or is under a curse.
- Whether it has Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability to Necrotic or Poison damage, and whether it has Immunity to disease.
- The ability in which it has the lowest saving throw bonus.

If two or more abilities tie for the lowest bonus, the DM chooses which you learn.

On a failure, you learn nothing, and you can't attempt to diagnose that creature again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

A creature you diagnose, automatically or with a successful check, becomes your **patient** until you diagnose another creature or finish a Long Rest. When you restore Hit Points to your patient with a Physician feature or a Physician spell, you can reroll any 1s on the healing dice. You must use the new rolls.

features.name: Treatment
features.text:
You can end an affliction with skill rather than magic. As a Utilize action, you can expend one use of a Healer's Kit and make an Intelligence (Medicine) check to treat your patient, who must be within your reach. The DC depends on what you are treating:

| Treatment | DC |
|---|---|
| End the Poisoned condition | 10 |
| End the Blinded or Deafened condition (if not permanent) | 12 |
| Cure one disease | 13 |
| End the Paralyzed condition | 15 |
| Remove one level of Exhaustion (once per creature per Long Rest) | 15 |

A disease you cure with Treatment is beaten the slow way, and the creature can't catch that disease again.

On a success, the chosen effect ends; if a spell or other ongoing effect imposed the condition, that effect ends on the creature. Either way, the use of the Healer's Kit is spent, and you can't attempt the same treatment on that creature again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Physician Subclass
features.text: You gain a Physician subclass of your choice, the specialty that shapes your practice: Chirurgeon, Combat Medic, Doctor, Hedge Witch, Immortalist, Neurologist, Plague Doctor, Surgeon, or Vitalist, each detailed after this class's description. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Physician level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Physician levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Steady Hands
features.text: A Short Rest now returns Prowess Dice by your character level, not your Physician level: all of them at levels 5–10, half your maximum (round up) at levels 11–16, and one from level 17. A Long Rest always returns all of them.

features.name: Bedside Manner
features.text: Your care makes rest more restorative. If you are conscious and within 30 feet of a creature when it spends Hit Point Dice during a Short Rest, that creature adds your Intelligence modifier to each Hit Point Die it spends during that rest. A creature can't benefit from more than one Physician's Bedside Manner during the same rest.

features.name: Vitals
features.text:
Once on each of your turns when you use Healing Prowess on your patient, you can use Diagnosis on a different creature as part of the same Bonus Action, or as part of the same attack if a feature lets you use Healing Prowess without spending a Bonus Action. This doesn't change your patient.

You also have Advantage on saving throws against disease and against the Poisoned condition.

features.name: Constitution of Iron
features.text: You have Immunity to disease and to the Poisoned condition, and you have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition.

features.name: Resuscitation
features.text: When you restore Hit Points to a creature that has 0 Hit Points, it regains additional Hit Points equal to your Physician level, and it can stand up from Prone without spending any of its movement.

features.name: Standing Orders
features.text: Once on each of your turns, when you take the Magic action to cast a Physician spell of level 1 or higher, you can also take one Bonus Action granted by a Physician feature as part of that action, without spending your Bonus Action. This can be Healing Prowess on a creature you touch, but not through an option your subclass adds to it (such as Vital Stream's range, Rip Life, Reflex, Miasma, either subclass's Under the Knife (Chirurgeon or Surgeon), or a medicated shot). A feature that only expends a Prowess Die, such as Ill Wish, Blood Price, the Bellows, or Stimulant, is allowed, and so is Exchange, which spends a Hit Point Die. You can't use this to cast a spell.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

features.name: Attending Physician
features.text:
When you roll Initiative, you regain one expended Prowess Die.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself would die (by failing its third Death Saving Throw, by taking damage that reduces it to 0 Hit Points with remaining damage equal to or exceeding its Hit Point maximum, or by an effect that kills it outright), you can take a Reaction to prevent its death. The creature instead drops to 0 Hit Points and is Stable, and it then regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended). Once you use this Reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Theatre Training
features.text: Your instrument is a Saw. You gain training with Medium armor and Shields, and proficiency with the following Martial weapons: the Battleaxe, Glaive, Greataxe, Greatsword, Halberd, Longsword, and Scimitar. The Saw is any of those weapons, or a Handaxe or Sickle, and you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells. You also gain weapon mastery: you can use the mastery properties of two kinds of Slashing weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, and whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds you chose.

features.name: Under the Knife
features.text:
When you hit a creature with your Saw in melee, you can use Healing Prowess on yourself as part of the same attack, without spending a Bonus Action: expend one Prowess Die and regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled (you don't add your Intelligence modifier). The work is on you as much as on them. When you do, if the creature you hit is Large or smaller, you can push it 10 feet away from you, or it must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Prone condition.

You can do this once on each of your turns, but not if you've already used Healing Prowess this turn, and if you do, you can't use Healing Prowess again until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Amputation
features.text:
You learn to take a limb, which you can do to an enemy or for a patient.

*In a fight.* When you hit a creature with your Saw in melee, you can expend one Prowess Die to take a limb instead of using Under the Knife on that hit. This counts as your use of Under the Knife for the turn: you can't do both on the same turn, you can't do it if you've already used Healing Prowess this turn, and you can't use Healing Prowess again until the start of your next turn. The creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the limb you chose crippled. On a Critical Hit, it fails automatically. If you take an arm, the creature drops whatever it was holding in that hand and has Disadvantage on attack rolls it makes with that limb (if its attacks don't name a limb, the DM chooses which of them use it); if you take a leg, its Speed is halved and it has the Prone condition. These effects last for 1 minute; the creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending them on a success. Only a limb taken on a table is gone for good. A creature that has Immunity to Slashing damage, or that has no such limb, is unaffected. Once a creature fails this saving throw, you can't take a limb this way again until you finish a Short or Long Rest; on a successful save the Prowess Die is still expended.

*On a table.* Outside combat, you can spend 1 minute removing a limb from a creature within your reach that is willing, or that has the Incapacitated condition and isn't hostile to you. No check is required. One disease, poison, curse, or other ongoing effect confined to that limb ends; whether an effect is so confined is the DM's judgment. The creature takes 2d10 Slashing damage that can't be reduced or prevented, gains one level of Exhaustion, and loses the limb until it is restored by *Regenerate* or comparable magic. A creature that has lost an arm can hold only one object at a time and can't wield a two-handed weapon, or a Shield and a weapon at once. A creature that has lost a leg has its Speed halved and needs a cane or crutch to move unless it has a prosthetic leg; it falls Prone after it takes the Dash action, and it has Disadvantage on Dexterity checks made to keep its balance.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Field Hospital
features.text:
When you cast a Physician spell with a range of Self that creates an Emanation or other area centered on you (such as *Aura of Vitality*, *Aura of Life*, *Aura of Purity*, *Antilife Shell*, or *Circle of Power*), the area's radius increases by 10 feet. When you regain Hit Points from such a spell that you are concentrating on, you regain additional Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier, once per turn.

In addition, while you are concentrating on such a spell, you can use Healing Prowess on any creature in its area, rather than only a creature you touch.

features.name: The Bellows
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one Prowess Die to work the bellows in a 15-foot Cone originating from you. Each willing creature of your choice in the Cone spends one of its Hit Point Dice and regains Hit Points as if it had spent that die at the end of a Short Rest, adding your Intelligence modifier to the roll. A creature that has no Hit Point Dice remaining gains no benefit. A creature that has no Hit Point Dice of its own, as most monsters don't, instead regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended). A creature can't be affected by your Bellows again until it finishes a Long Rest.

features.name: Theatre Closed
features.text: When a creature within 10 feet of you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to declare the theatre closed. Until the start of your next turn, each creature within 10 feet of you that you choose when you take the Reaction, including the triggering creature, can't be reduced below 1 Hit Point. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Combat Medic
subclasses.lead: You traded raw magical healing for martial versatility, and you go where the wounded are: the breach, the boarding party, the ambush on the caravan road. Your arrows and knives can heal your allies or cripple your enemies, and when a friend goes down, your next shot is already in the air.

features.name: Field Training
features.text:
You gain training with Medium armor and Shields, and proficiency with Martial weapons. You can also use any weapon you are proficient with as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells.

**Camp Physic.** When your company makes camp, you can site it: the water drawn upstream, the latrines dug down, the sick kept apart, and the food kept dry. In a camp you've sited, members of your company have Advantage on saving throws against natural diseases they would catch there. You also know how armies live: you can read a camp, a garrison, or a column on the march and tell how well fed, how sick, and how close to mutiny it is.

**Weapon Mastery.** Your training includes weapon mastery. You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longbows and Daggers. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

features.name: Arrows of Healing and Plague
features.text:
You can carry your medicine on a projectile. When you take the Attack action and make a ranged attack with a Ranged weapon or a weapon that has the Thrown property, you can expend one Prowess Die to make one of the attacks a **medicated shot**. Only one attack per Attack action can be a medicated shot. When you do so, choose one of the following:

- **Arrow of Healing.** Instead of making an attack roll, the shot automatically hits a creature of your choice that you can see within the weapon's normal range. The creature takes no damage from the shot and regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier. The shot triggers no effect that happens on a hit, such as a weapon's mastery property.
- **Arrow of Plague.** Make the attack roll as normal. On a hit, the target takes extra Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die, and it can't regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn.

The ammunition or thrown weapon is expended as normal. A medicated shot counts as using your Healing Prowess feature, though it doesn't use your Bonus Action. You can't make a medicated shot if you've already used Healing Prowess this turn, and once you make one, you can't use Healing Prowess again until the start of your next turn, except through Combat Shield.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Combat Shield
features.text:
When a creature you can see within the normal range of a Ranged or Thrown weapon you are wielding is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to make an Arrow of Healing at that creature, expending a Prowess Die and ammunition as normal.

Whenever you restore Hit Points to a creature that has 0 Hit Points, you and that creature each gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus plus your Intelligence modifier, and the creature can stand up from Prone without spending any of its movement.

features.name: Field Pharmacology
features.text:
You can lace your projectiles. When you make an Arrow of Plague, you can expend a second Prowess Die to add one of the following agents. On a hit, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer the agent's effect until the end of its next turn. If the target is your patient, it instead makes the saving throw using the ability in which you learned it has the lowest saving throw bonus.

- **Sedative.** The target has the Incapacitated condition. The effect ends early if the target takes damage after the shot that applied it.
- **Blinding Agent.** The target has the Blinded condition.
- **Paralytic.** The target's Speed becomes 0, and it can't take Reactions.

You also gain the following benefits:

- **Spreading Draught.** When an Arrow of Plague hits a creature, or an Arrow of Healing restores Hit Points to one, each other creature of your choice within 5 feet of that creature regains Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. (With Multi-Shot, choose one of the two creatures.)
- **Multi-Shot.** When you make an Arrow of Healing, you can expend two Prowess Dice instead of one. If you do, the shot heals two creatures of your choice within the weapon's normal range, each regaining Hit Points equal to one of the expended dice, rolled for it, plus your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Stimulant
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend two Prowess Dice to stimulate one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. For 1 minute (you must maintain Concentration on it, as if on a spell), the creature has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and once on each of its turns when it hits a creature with an attack roll or damages one with a spell, it can add one roll of your Prowess Die to the damage (no die is expended). Only one creature can be stimulated by you at a time; stimulating a second creature ends the effect on the first.

features.name: Line of Fire
features.text: Your medicated shots ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover. In addition, you can make a medicated shot against a creature you can't see if a creature that you can see and that is friendly to you is within 5 feet of it. From Physician level 17, when you roll Initiative and have no Prowess Dice, you regain one expended Prowess Die.

subclasses.name: Doctor
subclasses.lead: If a stranger pictures a Physician, they picture a Doctor. Your dedication to the healing arts is second to none. You link your patients in chains of vital current, heal and bolster them in the middle of a fight, and step through the air to whichever of them needs you when someone decides you make a good target.

features.name: Vital Stream
features.text:
You learn to channel a stream of vitalizing energy through your focus. As a Bonus Action, you can create a **link** to a willing creature you can see. If you have no chain, the link runs from you to a creature within 30 feet of you; otherwise, it runs from the last creature in your chain to a creature within 30 feet of that creature. You and the creatures you link form your **chain**, in the order they were linked; you are always its first link and don't count against its limit. Your chain can include up to two creatures other than you. This number increases to three at Physician level 6, four at level 10, and five at level 14.

A link ends if the two creatures it connects are ever more than 60 feet apart, if either of them drops to 0 Hit Points (unless you use Stand Back on it), if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you end it (no action required). Links otherwise last until you finish a Long Rest. A creature is in your chain only while an unbroken sequence of links connects it to you; if a link ends, any creature no longer connected to you leaves your chain.

While you have a chain, you gain the following benefits:

- **Range.** You can use Healing Prowess on any creature in your chain, rather than only a creature you touch. Only Healing Prowess travels the chain this way; a spell you cast doesn't, unless a feature says it does.
- **Heal or Bolster.** When you use Healing Prowess on a creature in your chain, you can choose to have it gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier instead of regaining Hit Points. A creature that gains Temporary Hit Points this way also gains a +1 bonus to the next attack roll or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.
- **Triage.** When you use Healing Prowess on a creature in your chain, one creature of your choice that is adjacent to it in the chain gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.
- **Stand Back.** When a creature in your chain is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to use Healing Prowess on it, and its link doesn't end. Once you use it, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Practice
features.text: In any settlement, you can set up a practice with a day's work and a room. While you practice, you earn a comfortable living, and patients talk: after a day of practice in a place, you know its gossip, who is sick, who is pregnant, who is drinking, who has been beaten, and who is paying for it. A household that has called you to a bedside will let you in again.

features.name: House Call
features.text: When you would take damage, or when a hostile creature ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction and expend one Prowess Die to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of a creature in your chain that is within 30 feet of you. You still take the damage that triggered the Reaction.

features.name: On Your Feet
features.text:
You can cast *Revivify* on a creature in your chain, even if you don't have it prepared, without expending a spell slot or providing Material components. For this purpose, a creature that was in your chain when it dropped to 0 Hit Points and has since died is treated as still linked for 1 minute after its death. A creature you return to life this way regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended), instead of 1 Hit Point. Once you cast *Revivify* in this way, you can't cast it this way again until you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, you are no longer limited in how often you can use Stand Back; you can use it whenever you have a Reaction and a Prowess Die to spend.

features.name: Total Routing
features.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you cast a Physician spell of level 1 or higher that restores Hit Points, each creature in your chain, including you, regains Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. Your Triage feature can now grant its Temporary Hit Points to any creature in your chain, not only one adjacent to the target.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to link that creature to the last creature in your chain (or to you, if your chain is empty); it needn't be willing, the 30-foot limit for making a link doesn't apply, and the link doesn't end for the creature's having 0 Hit Points. It counts against the number of creatures your chain can include; if your chain is already full, the link to the current last creature ends first.

subclasses.name: Hedge Witch
subclasses.lead: You learned the old ways of healing from a relative, a village healer, or someone else who knew that life costs life. You draw on the pain you and your allies receive, and you pay the price freely.

features.name: Rip Life
features.text: You learn to take vitality rather than give it. When you use Healing Prowess, you can rip it from a creature instead of touching an ally: choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. You, or one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself, then regain Hit Points equal to the damage dealt.

features.name: Cunning Folk
features.text: You know the remedies, charms, and taboos of any countryside you've lived in for a season. The people there who would never go to a Lanternhall doctor come to you, and they tell you what they'd never tell a priest. You can also look at a charm, a witch bottle, a poppet, or a hex sign and tell what it was made to do, whether it worked, and whether the hand that made it knew what it was doing.

features.name: Ill Wish
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one Prowess Die to curse one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be cursed until the end of your next turn. Choose one ability score when you curse the creature: while cursed, it has Disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws made with that ability. If the creature is your patient, it makes the saving throw against Ill Wish using the ability in which you learned it has the lowest saving throw bonus. The curse ends early if you use this feature on another creature, or if the target is affected by *Remove Curse* or a similar effect.

features.name: Communal Pain
features.text:
You learn to share what is done to you and yours. As a Magic action, you can expend one Prowess Die to raise an aura of shared suffering in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you for 1 minute. While the aura lasts, whenever a willing creature in the aura would take damage, the damage is instead divided as evenly as possible among that creature and every other willing creature in the aura that has more than half its Hit Points (any remainder goes to the original target). When one effect damages several willing creatures in the aura at once, total the damage and divide it once. Each creature applies its own Resistance, Vulnerability, and Immunity to its share, and the shares can't be redirected further. You can end the aura early at any time (no action required).

Every point of damage you take from hostile creatures while the aura is active, including shares divided onto you, is stored as **Pain**. You can store Pain up to three times your Physician level; any excess is lost. Stored Pain is lost when the aura ends.

As a Magic action, you can release your stored Pain in one of two ways:

- **Retribution.** One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes Necrotic damage equal to the Pain released, or half as much on a successful Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.
- **Restitution.** One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to the Pain released.

Releasing Pain reduces your stored Pain to 0.

features.name: Blood Price
features.text:
You can pay for healing with your own blood. While your Communal Pain aura is active, you can take a Bonus Action to expend one Prowess Die and roll it. You take Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled, which can't be reduced or prevented and isn't divided by your Communal Pain aura, and each other willing creature in the aura regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled. Damage you take this way is stored as Pain.

In addition, your Ill Wish now lasts for 1 minute (you must maintain Concentration on it, as if on a spell), you can have up to two creatures cursed by it at once (cursing a third ends the oldest curse), and a creature cursed by your Ill Wish takes extra Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier the first time each turn it takes damage from your Rip Life or a Physician spell you cast.

features.name: Threefold
features.text:
When you release Pain, you can divide it among up to three creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself, choosing Retribution or Restitution for each. A creature cursed by your Ill Wish that takes Retribution damage takes an additional amount equal to your Intelligence modifier. You can store Pain up to five times your Physician level, and you can release Pain as a Bonus Action.

In addition, your Communal Pain aura becomes a 20-foot Emanation.

subclasses.name: Immortalist
subclasses.lead:
Instead of using your magic on others, you turned it on yourself, to see how far you could go. Now it draws on your vital energy and turns it into the forces of nature. The only true limit to your power is your own body.

*For a Jekyll-and-Hyde campaign, see the optional rule The Monster Within, later in this class description.*

features.name: The Font Within
features.text:
You find the Font: the same source of life that clerics receive from their gods and druids from nature. There is only one, but you have found it inside your own body rather than outside it, and you draw on it from there. It gives you a second way to pay for your magic.

**Draw on the Font.** You keep your spell slots and cast with them as normal. In addition, when you cast a Physician spell of level 1 through 5, you can draw on the Font instead, up to a total number of spell levels equal to your Physician level between Long Rests (your **Font limit**): you spend a number of Hit Point Dice equal to the spell's level instead of expending a spell slot. Only Hit Point Dice you gained from Physician levels can be spent this way. Hit Point Dice spent this way are expended without being rolled and don't restore Hit Points. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended Hit Point Die that you spent drawing on the Font. While you have this feature, a Long Rest restores only half your total Hit Point Dice (minimum of one), not all of them. If you cast the spell with a higher-level slot's effect, you spend Hit Point Dice equal to the level at which you cast it, which can be no higher than the highest level of spell slot you have. You can't draw on the Font to cast a spell of level 6 or higher. Drawing on the Font counts as expending a spell slot for the rule that you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell on a turn.

> **The Cost Shows**
>
> A day of heavy casting is followed by thinner days, and the character won't feel it until they try to rest. As the DM, show the cost before then: fatigue, unsteady hands, a drawn face. A Physician who has spent half their Hit Point Dice by noon should look like it.

**Symbiosis.** Drawing on the Font changes what your body needs and what it can survive. You gain the following as you reach the listed Physician levels:

- **Level 5.** You add *Fly* to your spellbook. It counts as a Physician spell for you and doesn't count against the spells you add to your spellbook when you gain a level.
- **Level 9.** You stop aging, and you can't be aged magically.
- **Level 13.** You no longer need to eat, drink, or breathe.
- **Level 17.** When you drop to 0 Hit Points, you are automatically Stable, and you don't make Death Saving Throws. Damage still causes Death Saving Throw failures; you become Stable again after each one.

features.name: Font-Touched
features.text: Choose one spell from the Cleric spell list of a level for which the Physician Features table gives you spell slots at your Physician level. The spell can't be one that produces a creature or anything else that takes its own actions. The Font is your own life, not anyone else's. The spell counts as a Physician spell for you, is added to your spellbook, and is always prepared; it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You choose an additional spell this way at Physician levels 6, 10, and 14.

features.name: Attuned Energy
features.text:
Choose a damage type: Cold, Fire, Lightning, Psychic, or Radiant. This is your **attuned energy**: the form your own vitality takes when you push it outward. Fire is your metabolism let loose, the vital heat every living body burns to stay alive. Lightning is the signal that runs your nerves. Cold is the slowed heart and the held breath, and the rime that follows. Radiant is your own life burning as bright as the sun, and everything near you feels the heat of it. Psychic is the will that moves your flesh, sent to move something else: a column of wrong.

A Physician's harm is Necrotic. Yours no longer has to be. When you cast a Physician spell that deals Necrotic damage, you can have it deal your attuned damage type instead; the spell is otherwise unchanged, and what anyone watching sees is your energy, not the spell's.

You also work in your energy directly. Choose one cantrip that deals your attuned damage type, from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, Physician, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard spell list. It counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know. In addition, add to your spellbook one spell of each level from 1 through 5 that deals your attuned damage type, chosen from those spell lists; you add each spell when you reach a Physician level at which you can cast it. These spells count as Physician spells for you and don't count against the spells you add to your spellbook when you gain a level. If no spell of a given level deals your attuned damage type, you can instead choose an additional spell of any lower level that does.

> **Suggested Attunements**
>
> These are working sets: a cantrip, then one spell per level from 1 to 5. You aren't bound to them. Any spell that deals your energy, from those seven spell lists, is a legal pick.
>
> **Fire.** *Fire Bolt*, then *Burning Hands · Scorching Ray · Fireball · Wall of Fire · Flame Strike.*
>
> **Cold.** *Ray of Frost*, which also drops the target's Speed, then *Armor of Agathys · Dragon's Breath · Cold Storage · Ice Storm · Cone of Cold.* (Take *Ice Knife* at level 1 instead if you want something to throw.)
>
> **Lightning.** *Shocking Grasp*, which keeps the target from making Opportunity Attacks, then *Witch Bolt · Convulsion · Lightning Bolt · Call Lightning · Defibrillation.* (No level 4 spell in the *Player's Handbook* deals Lightning, so *Call Lightning* is the level 4 pick. *Arc*, a new Sorcerer and Wizard spell (see A Spell From Another List, later in this class), is another level 3 choice: a Bonus Action teleport instead of the line.)
>
> **Radiant.** *Sacred Flame*, which ignores cover, then *Guiding Bolt · Moonbeam · Spirit Guardians · Guardian of Faith · Flame Strike.*
>
> **Psychic.** *Mind Sliver*, which takes a d4 off the target's next save, then *Dissonant Whispers · Mind Spike · Hysteria · Phantasmal Killer · Synaptic Static.*

features.name: Life-Fused Casting
features.text:
When you cast a level 1+ spell that deals your attuned damage type, or use a Bonus Action to deal damage with such a spell you are concentrating on, you can expend one Prowess Die as part of that action and choose one of the following:

- One target of the spell takes extra damage of your attuned type equal to the number rolled.
- One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

You can't use Life-Fused Casting on a spell cast from an item's charges.

features.name: Transfusion
features.text:
You learn to move vital energy between forms, and from your own body into another's.

**Exchange.** As a Bonus Action, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to regain one expended Prowess Die. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

**Perfusion.** Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you can touch another willing creature and route the Font into its spellcasting. Choose one:

- *Draw on its behalf.* Spend from 1 to 5 Physician Hit Point Dice. The creature regains one expended spell slot whose level equals the number of Hit Point Dice you spent. This counts as drawing on the Font: the Hit Point Dice count against the total you can draw between Long Rests.
- *Give what you carry.* Expend one of your own spell slots. The creature regains one expended spell slot of the same level.

The creature can't regain a spell slot of a level higher than the highest it can normally cast, and it must have expended a slot of that level to regain it. The creature regains a spell slot, not any other resource.

features.name: Conduit
features.text: You have Resistance to your attuned damage type. In addition, when you cast a level 1+ spell that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures, expending a spell slot or Hit Point Dice to do so, you can cause one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself to take damage of your attuned type equal to your Intelligence modifier plus the level of the spell slot expended or the number of Hit Point Dice spent to cast it. This doesn't work with a spell cast from an item's charges.

features.name: Rebirth
features.text: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you instead drop to 1 Hit Point. Each other creature within 10 feet of you either takes 2d10 damage of your attuned type or regains 2d10 Hit Points; you choose for each creature. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Neurologist
subclasses.lead: Your medicine works on the nerves, and through them on the mind. Thomas Willis gave the discipline its name in Oxford four years ago, and it's still the least understood of them. Neurologists work on the current that runs through every living body, offering solace to allies and torment to enemies.

features.name: Reading the Nerves
features.text:
You learn to read the body's wiring. When you use Diagnosis on a creature, automatically or with a successful check, you also learn whether any effect on its mind, such as a charm, a fear, a compulsion, or a voice, is the creature's own, the work of a spell or similar magical effect, or the influence of another creature; if the source is a creature you can see, you learn which one.

Add the following to your Treatment table:

| Treatment | DC |
|---|---|
| End the Charmed or Frightened condition | 12 |
| End the Stunned condition | 15 |

You also gain proficiency in the Insight skill if you don't already have it, and you learn the *Mind Sliver* cantrip, which counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know.

**Neurologist Spells.** When you reach a Physician level specified in the Neurologist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. Each counts as a Physician spell for you and is added to your spellbook.

| Physician Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Dissonant Whispers*, *Mind Spike* |
| 5 | *Hypnotic Pattern*, *Tiny Hut* |
| 7 | *Compulsion*, *Phantasmal Killer* |
| 9 | *Dominate Person*, *Modify Memory* |

features.name: Reflex
features.text:
You can send your medicine along the nerves instead of through your hands. When you use Healing Prowess, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself instead of a creature you touch. The creature regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

**Nerve Sheathing.** A nerve carries better when it is wrapped. When you use Reflex, the creature can choose one of the following: it regains its Reaction if it has used it since the start of its last turn, or it can immediately move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. A creature that has benefited from Nerve Sheathing can't do so again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: The Quiet Room
features.text: With an hour of treatment (a dark quiet room, running water, music, or talk), you can ease a creature's mind: one fear, panic, or mania that isn't magical leaves it for a day, and it sleeps that night. You can also tell, by watching a fit, whether it's a seizure, a possession, a curse, or a performance, and you can explain the difference to a cathedral in terms it can't easily dismiss.

features.name: Steady the Signal
features.text:
When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw against the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned condition, or against a spell or other effect that deals Psychic damage, you can take a Reaction and expend one Prowess Die to let it reroll the saving throw. It must use the new roll.

In addition, you can perform Treatment for the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned condition on your patient while you can see it within 30 feet of yourself, rather than only within your reach, and doing so doesn't expend a use of a Healer's Kit.

You also learn to press on the wire while a spell is traveling down it. When you cast a Physician spell that can give a creature the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Stunned, or Incapacitated condition, you can expend one Prowess Die as part of casting the spell. One target of the spell has Disadvantage on its saving throw against it.

features.name: Overload
features.text:
The first time a creature fails a saving throw against a given casting of a Physician spell that deals Psychic damage or that gives a creature the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Stunned, or Incapacitated condition, it takes extra Psychic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier, and it can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

In addition, you can cast *Haste* or *Slow* once without expending a spell slot, even if you don't have it prepared. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, once on each of your turns when you cast a Physician spell of level 1 or higher that deals Psychic damage or that can give a creature the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Stunned, or Incapacitated condition, you and each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: The Body Electric
features.text:
The whole wire answers you. You have Immunity to the Paralyzed and Stunned conditions, and magic can't reduce your Speed. Your patient, if it isn't hostile to you, has Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions while it is within 30 feet of you.

In addition, when you use Reflex, the creature can instead immediately take one of these actions: the Attack action (one weapon attack only), the Dash action, the Disengage action, the Hide action, or the Utilize action. This counts as its use of Nerve Sheathing. A creature can benefit from this once, and can't do so again until it finishes a Long Rest.

features.name: Miasma
features.text:
You learn to carry your medicine on the air. When you use Healing Prowess, you can release it as a cloud instead of a touch: choose a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself. A 10-foot-radius Sphere of restorative vapor appears centered on that point and lasts until the end of the turn. One creature of your choice in the area regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier. Each other creature of your choice in the area that has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. Each creature of your choice in the area has Advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

You also gain proficiency in the Nature skill if you don't already have it, you have Resistance to Poison damage, and you can't transmit a disease you carry.

features.name: Bill of Health
features.text: You know the quarantine law and practice of any port, city, or border you're in: how long it holds arrivals, what passes it accepts, and how its cordon is kept. Health boards, harbor masters, and quarantine officers recognize you as one of theirs. You can issue a bill of health for a person or a ship you've examined and found clean, and those officers will honor it. (Forging one is outside this feature.)

features.name: Pathology
features.text: When you cast a Physician spell that deals Necrotic or Poison damage, you can expend one Prowess Die as part of casting the spell to deal extra damage of that type to one target of the spell equal to the number rolled.

features.name: Purge
features.text:
Your treatment reaches everyone in the cloud. When you use Miasma, you can take a Utilize action on the same turn to perform Treatment on every willing creature in that Miasma's area at once, whether or not it is your patient, making a single Intelligence (Medicine) check and expending a single use of a Healer's Kit. Each creature is treated for the same effect; a creature that has been treated for that effect since its last rest can't benefit, whether the earlier attempt succeeded or failed.

In addition, you can make your Miasma noxious. When you do, no creature regains Hit Points or gains Advantage from it; instead, each hostile creature in the area when it appears takes Poison damage equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die, or half as much on a successful Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. Once you make your Miasma noxious, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. From Physician level 10, you can do so twice between rests.

features.name: The Slow Way
features.text: You can tell, by Diagnosis or an hour's examination, which members of a household have had a disease and come through it the slow way, and so can't catch it again, and which were cured by magic and can. You can also nurse the slow way. When you tend a creature through a natural disease over a Long Rest, without ending it with a spell or a feature, it has Advantage on its saving throws against the disease until your next Long Rest; if it recovers, it can't catch that disease again. A disease ended by Treatment counts as the slow way too.

features.name: Outbreak
features.text:
Your afflictions spread. When a creature fails a saving throw against a level 1+ Physician spell you cast that deals Necrotic or Poison damage, or fails its saving throw against your noxious Miasma, it becomes **infected**. The infection is a disease. An infected creature can't regain Hit Points, and at the start of each of its turns it takes Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (you can choose for it to take none) and then makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the infection on a success. A creature of your choice that ends its turn within 5 feet of an infected creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or become infected. An infection ends after 1 minute if it hasn't ended sooner, and a creature whose infection ends can't be infected by this feature again for 1 minute. No more creatures can be infected at once than your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one); while that many are infected, no other creature becomes infected. Creatures that have Immunity to disease can't be infected, and your allies are never infected by this feature.

In addition, each creature that regains Hit Points from your Miasma has Resistance to Poison damage and can't be diseased until the end of its next turn.

**Tracing.** When you examine a creature that has a natural disease, you learn whom or what it caught the disease from, if that source is within a day's travel, and the route it took: the water, the air, a touch, the cloth, the food, or the vermin.

features.name: Doctor's Rounds
features.text:
The radius of your Miasma becomes 20 feet. In addition, each friendly creature within 10 feet of you has Advantage on Constitution saving throws and has Immunity to disease and to the Poisoned condition. From Physician level 17, when you roll Initiative and have no Prowess Dice, you regain one expended Prowess Die.

**Wide Berth.** You can walk into and out of a quarantined city, a cordon, or a pest house, and no guard stops you. A health officer anywhere will take your word on whether a house can be opened, a ship unloaded, or a body buried.

features.name: Theatre Training
features.text: Your instrument is a Scalpel. It is a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells rather than a weapon. You also learn the *Mage Hand* cantrip if you don't already know it. It counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know, and the spectral hand takes the shape of your instrument.

features.name: Under the Knife
features.text:
When you hit a creature with an incision (described below), you can use your Healing Prowess as part of the same attack, without spending a Bonus Action. You expend a Prowess Die as normal. The creature you heal can be any creature within 10 feet of you or within 10 feet of the target. If the target is your patient, it can't take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

You can use Healing Prowess this way once on each of your turns, but not if you've already used Healing Prowess this turn, and if you do, you can't use Healing Prowess again until the start of your next turn.

features.name: The Incision
features.text: As a Magic action, you can make an **incision**: a ranged spell attack using Intelligence against a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Force damage. This damage increases to 2d10 at Physician level 5, 3d10 at level 11, and 4d10 at level 17.

features.name: The Sharpest Cut
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can send your instrument to hover at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself, where it stays until you send it again, recall it as a Bonus Action, or have the Unconscious condition. It returns to you if it is ever more than 60 feet from you, and it can't be targeted by attacks, spells, or other effects.

While it hovers there, your incisions originate from the instrument rather than from you, and you can use Healing Prowess on any creature within 10 feet of it rather than only a creature you touch.

The hovering instrument can also do anything your *Mage Hand* could do (manipulate an object, open a door or a container, carry up to 10 pounds) using a Bonus Action, without your having to cast the spell.

features.name: The Sealed Table
features.text:
You add *Telekinesis* and *Resilient Sphere* to your spellbook. They count as Physician spells for you and are always prepared; they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

You also learn to seal the table. When you cast *Resilient Sphere*, you can choose to have it enclose you and one willing creature within 5 feet of you together, as though the two of you were a single Large creature. While you are enclosed together, you can perform Treatment on that creature and use Healing Prowess on it as normal; nothing else passes through the sphere in either direction, as the spell describes.

In addition, you can perform Treatment on your patient while it is within 10 feet of your hovering instrument, rather than only within your reach.

features.name: Theatre Closed
features.text: When a creature within 10 feet of you, or within 10 feet of your hovering instrument, would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to declare the theatre closed. Choose the point the triggering creature was within 10 feet of, you or the instrument. Until the start of your next turn, each creature within 10 feet of that point that you choose when you take the Reaction, including the triggering creature, can't be reduced below 1 Hit Point. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Book of the World
features.text:
