When you reach a Physician level specified in the Vitalist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared, and they are in your spellbook. They count as Physician spells for you and don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

| Physician Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Goodberry*, *Speak with Animals* |
| 5 | *Locate Animals or Plants*, *Speak with Plants* |
| 7 | *Locate Creature*, *Plant Growth* |
| 9 | *Commune with Nature*, *Reincarnate* |

features.name: Signatures
features.text:
You gain proficiency in the Nature skill and with the Herbalism Kit; if you already have either, choose another skill from the Physician's skill list or another tool. By handling a plant, a stone, a fungus, or a part of an animal for 1 minute, you learn its virtues: whether it's poisonous and what it would do, what it heals or harms, and whether it could serve as a component for a spell you know. Given an hour in any place where things grow, you can find the simples for an ordinary remedy, a dye, or a poison.

**Diagnose a Place.** You can use Diagnosis on a place you stand in (a field, a well, a wood, a house): you learn whether it is blighted, poisoned, diseased, or cursed, and whether it is thin ground (*Life on the Border*).

**Treat a Place.** You can use Treatment on a place you have diagnosed. It takes 1 hour and a use of a Healer's Kit, and the DC is the same as for the affliction in a creature (cure a disease for a blighted field or a sickly herd, end the Poisoned condition for a poisoned well). On a success, the place mends over the next few days. A curse needs magic, as it would in a patient.

**Respectable.** Your magic is natural magic, and to anyone trained to look it reads that way. You have Advantage on any ability check to convince an official, a licensing examiner, or an inquisitor that your magic is lawful.

features.name: The World's Pulse
features.text:
You feel the pulse of the living world around you. You know the location of every living creature within 30 feet of yourself, and whether each is unharmed, injured, Bloodied, or near death. A creature that is hidden from you or has the Invisible condition can't hide its location from your sense, and you aren't surprised by a living creature within range when you roll Initiative. Undead and Constructs have no pulse: you sense them only as a gap where the life around them stops, which is often how you find them. The range becomes 60 feet at Physician level 10.

This sense needs no sight, and it works through walls, but not through more than a few feet of stone or a sheet of lead.

features.name: The Wheel Turns
features.text:
When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you, to which you have restored Hit Points since your last Long Rest, drops to 0 Hit Points but isn't killed outright, you can take a Reaction: the creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead and regains Hit Points equal to your Physician level. Every green thing within 60 feet of you goes through a year in a moment: it buds, flowers, fruits, and drops its leaves. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**The Great Chain of Being.** You know at a glance a creature's type and whether it is a Hidden creature (*Life on the Border*, Introduction, The Hidden, in the rules).

> **Playing a Vitalist**
>
> Heal, and feel it come back: every time you mend someone else, you mend a little yourself. Don't worry about overhealing; whatever a creature can't hold goes on to the next one who needs it, and from 10th level it stays as a cushion. When a blade is about to land on someone near you, let the ground take part of it. Out of a fight, you're the one who can diagnose a field, a well, or a herd, and treat it. Open the windows.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in the Medicine skill, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Physician Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in the Medicine skill, and training with Light armor. Gain the Physician's level 1 features, which are listed in the Physician Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add all your Physician levels, as you would Wizard levels.

data.name: Revelator
data.blurb: Half caster. The planes of the Plenum.

The Border Ethereal, Ethereal Stride, Fighting Style, Visiting Spirit

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
You draw the power of the cosmos through yourself. See the Player's Handbook for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Revelator spells, which appear in the Revelator spell list later in the class's description.

**Spell Slots.** The Revelator Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Revelator spells. *Healing Word* and *Protection from Evil and Good* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Revelator levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Revelator Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Revelator spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Revelator spell for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Revelator spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use Cartographer's Tools, a token carried back from a spirit voyage, or a weapon with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus for your Revelator spells.

features.name: Vistas
features.text:
*Your glimpse of the greater cosmology awakened something within you, something you can now share with others.*

**Favor.** Each Revelation you know grants you its plane's Favor once between rests: you call on the Favor to open a vista. Your pathway's level 3 Revelation is the plane you know best, and it grants its Favor twice. Some features let a plane grant its Favor more often, but no plane grants it more than three times between rests. When a feature lets you **regain a Favor**, choose a plane that has already granted its Favor: it can grant it once more. You regain every Favor when you finish a Short or Long Rest. Most Favors open a vista; a few features, such as Ethereal Stride, call on a Favor without opening one.

**Opening a Vista.** As a Bonus Action, you call on the Favor of a Revelation you know and open a vista at a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself, and **let in an Influence**: choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of the vista (it can be you). That Revelation's Influence takes effect on it. From Revelator level 2, a vista can call a spirit instead (Visiting Spirit).

**Your Open Vista.** A vista stays open for 1 minute, until you open another one, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition. Your open vista is the one you opened most recently that is still open; it sets the damage of your Planar Strike.

When a vista or its Influence calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC. Whenever a Revelator feature uses your spell save DC or spell attack modifier, it means the ones you use for Revelator spells.

> **Tracking Favors**
>
> Give each plane you know a box, and two for your earth end (more from walked planes at 9th level, Mount Olympus's Arete, or items, never more than three). Tick a box when a plane grants its Favor. Regaining a Favor erases a tick; a Short or Long Rest erases them all.

**Revelations.** Revelations are the planes you know. Each gives one Spirit Aspect and one Influence. Some are granted by your features; you choose others from the planes your training has reached. The full set is in the Cosmography later in the class's description. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one Revelation you chose with another you're eligible for. Revelations granted by features can't be replaced.

features.name: Planar Strike
features.text:
When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a Planar Strike: a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of yourself, or a ranged spell attack against a creature within 60 feet of yourself. On a hit, the target takes damage equal to the dice shown in the Planar Strike column of the Revelator Features table, plus your Wisdom modifier for each of those dice (so 2d12 adds twice your Wisdom modifier). You can make only one Planar Strike on each of your turns. Planar Strike is magical but isn't a spell; you need a free hand or a hand holding your Spellcasting Focus to make it.

**The Plane's Power.** The damage is the type the Cosmography gives your open vista's Revelation. If you have no vista open, it's Force damage.

features.name: Echoes
features.text:
*The closest planes to the world are your first lessons.*

You know two Revelations: the Hidden and the Ghostlands.

features.name: Traveler's Arms
features.text:
*You know how to handle yourself on the road.*

Your training includes weapon mastery. You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Spears and Light Crossbows. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

features.name: The Border Ethereal
features.text:
*You branch out into the tangible spirit of all things, the Ethereal Plane.*

You know the Revelation of the Border Ethereal.

**Veilsight.** You can see into the Border Ethereal within 60 feet of yourself, and you can speak with spirits and ghosts as if you shared a language.

features.name: Ethereal Stride
features.text:
*Your familiarity with the Ethereal blossoms.*

As a Bonus Action, you can call on the Favor of the Border Ethereal, or of the Deep Ethereal if you know it, to step into the Border Ethereal until the end of your turn. While there, you can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, and creatures on the Material Plane can't see you unless they can see into the Ethereal. You can affect and be affected only by things in the Ethereal Plane. Ethereal Stride doesn't open a vista.

**Guiding.** You can bring one willing creature you touch. It enters the Border Ethereal with you, moves with you, staying within 5 feet of you, and returns when you do.

You return to the Material Plane when the stride ends. If you would arrive inside an object or creature, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 1d10 Force damage. The same applies to any creature you guide.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.text:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see the Player's Handbook). Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

**Planar Adept.** You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Revelator spell list. *Guidance* and *Message* are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Revelator spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Revelator level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the Revelator spell list.

features.name: Visiting Spirit
features.text:
When you open a vista, you can **call a spirit** instead of letting in an Influence. A spirit of that plane steps through into an unoccupied space at or next to the vista. It uses the Visiting Spirit stat block, with that Revelation's Spirit Aspect.

You can have one spirit at a time, and it doesn't require Concentration. It stays for 1 hour, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, until you call another spirit, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition. If a spirit you called drops to 0 Hit Points, you can't call any spirit again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

**A Guest, Not a Soldier.** The spirit is an ally to you and your companions, but it doesn't fight: it can't make attack rolls, and it doesn't deal damage. In combat, it shares your Initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. You decide its movement, its Reaction, and its action; on its turn it can take the Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Search, or Utilize action.

**Commanding the Spirit.** While the spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can command it with a Bonus Action, and the vista that calls it also commands it; letting in an Influence doesn't. When commanded, the spirit uses its Aspect's power at once, as part of your Bonus Action, and then takes no action on its turn.

**Speaking Across.** While the spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. As a Bonus Action, you can see through its eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining any special senses it has.

> **Visiting Spirit**
>
> *Small or Medium creature (your choice) of the type its Spirit Aspect names, Neutral*
>
> **AC** 12 + your Wisdom modifier
>
> **HP** 5 + your Revelator level
>
> **Speed** 30 ft.
>
> | STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | 10 | 14 | 10 | 10 | 12 | 10 |
>
> **Saving Throws** use your saving throw bonuses
>
> **Senses** Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11
>
> **Languages** understands the languages you know
>
> ***Aspect.*** It gains the Spirit Aspect of the Revelation that called it, including its creature type. Effects that depend on creature type, such as *Protection from Evil and Good* or *Banishment*, treat the spirit as that type. When an Aspect calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

> **For the DM: The Spirit Is a Guide**
>
> A Visiting Spirit helps, scouts, and carries, and it isn't there to take hits for the party. Play it like a familiar: enemies swat it when it's in their way or when it's obviously helping, and otherwise ignore it.

features.name: Revelator Pathway
features.text: You gain a Revelator subclass of your choice: the pathway that called you on your spirit voyage. The Path of Judgment, the Oceanus, Mount Olympus, the Styx, and Yggdrasil are detailed after this class's description. Each pathway spans the Veil from earth to sky: at level 3 you learn its earth end, where it touches the Deep Ethereal, and at levels 7 and 15 its Outer Planes. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your pathway's features that are of your Revelator level or lower; Yggdrasil also has one at level 5.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Revelator levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: The Near Planes
features.text:
*Your soul expands to encompass the energetic planar sources.*

You learn one Revelation of your choice from the Cosmography's near planes: Positive Energy, Negative Energy, the Deep Ethereal, or the Elemental Planes.

features.name: The Crossings
features.text:
*The spirit and soul meet the mind.*

You know the Revelation of the Astral.

**Wayfinder.** You can't become lost by magical means, and you always know the direction to the nearest portal, curtain, or color pool on the plane you're on. You have Advantage on Intelligence checks to recall lore about the planes and their inhabitants.

features.name: Guide's Hand
features.text:
*Your experience allows you to help others traveling with you.*

**Many Travelers.** When you use Ethereal Stride, you can guide a number of willing creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one), each of whom you touch or who is within 5 feet of a creature you guide.

**Hold the Threshold.** When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself rolls a Death Saving Throw and fails (not a failure caused by taking damage), you can take a Reaction to turn the failure into a success (on a roll of 1, one of its two failures). You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Reach Beyond
features.text:
*You can push through to the deepest, most well-guarded parts of reality, if you're brave enough.*

Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can open a vista without calling on a Favor, reaching instead for any Revelation in the Cosmography that you don't know. You can do this even when every plane's Favor is spent. You can also reach past the Cosmography, toward what it leaves out: a single layer or realm, such as the efreet's city in the Plane of Fire or a god's hall in Valhalla; a ruler and their court, such as an archfey, Yama with his scribe, the Jade Emperor in his palace, the lord of the deepest circle of the Nine, or a demon lord in their layer; or what lies between and beyond, such as the dead gods adrift in the Astral, the crossroads of the Middle World, or the Far Realm. When you do, the vista calls a spirit or lets in an Influence, and the DM decides what comes through from that place's nature: an Aspect or an Influence of about the same power as the Cosmography's.

**The Strain.** The further you reach, the more passes through you, and the body you left behind has to bear it. Reaching a plane in the Cosmography costs you nothing more than its Attention. Reaching past the Cosmography forces you to make a Constitution saving throw: DC 15 for a particular layer or realm, or DC 20 for a god, a ruler, or the Far Realm. On a failed save, you take 6d6 Psychic damage (10d6 against DC 20); on a successful save, you take half as much damage only. If you fail the DC 20 save, you also have the Incapacitated condition until you finish a Short or Long Rest, as your spirit takes the long way home. Either way, the vista opens; you get what you reached for, and the vista and whatever came through it stay despite that Incapacitated condition.

**Attention.** A power of that plane notices you, and you have its Attention. The DM decides what the power guards and what it wants from you; it might call in a favor, pay you a visit, set you a test, or name a debt. Powers act from their nature, not from malice, but not necessarily kindly. The plane takes its due: the next time you finish a Short or Long Rest, one plane you called on (the DM's choice) doesn't regain its Favor until you finish your next rest. If you gained Attention more than once since your last rest, that many planes stay spent. While you have a power's Attention, using Reach Beyond on its plane again deepens the relationship rather than drawing new Attention.

features.name: Soul's Journey
features.text:
*Your soul never forgets your travels, for better and for worse.*

A Revelation you know is **walked** once you have been to that plane in the body, spent at least a Long Rest there, and come back. How you got there doesn't matter: by portal, by another's spell, by being taken, by walking in for the name of it, or by waking up there. The plane cares only that you stayed, and what it does to those who stay is the lesson (see "What the Walk Costs"). A plane you walked before you knew its Revelation is walked the moment you learn it.

A walked plane knows you: it grants its Favor twice between rests, as your pathway's earth end does. Walking the earth end itself adds nothing.

**The Hard Roads.** Seven places on the Wheel are walked by almost no one: Pandemonium, Tartarus, Asphodel, Gehenna, Acheron, Cocytus, and the Seven Gates. Walking one leaves a mark, whether or not you know its Revelation yet, and you keep it for the rest of your life:

- **Pandemonium.** The winds are quiet in you. You have Resistance to Psychic damage, and you can't have the Deafened condition.
- **Tartarus.** Nothing holds you. You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to avoid or end the Grappled, Restrained, and Paralyzed conditions, and you automatically succeed on checks made to escape a *Maze*. *Imprisonment* can't hold you for longer than 1 minute.
- **Asphodel.** Nothing drains you. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition, and your Hit Point maximum can't be reduced.
- **Gehenna.** Nothing is owed. You have Resistance to Fire damage, and effects that would reduce or prevent the Hit Points you regain don't apply to you.
- **Acheron.** The press doesn't take you. You have Advantage on saving throws made to maintain Concentration, and no spell or effect can make you attack a creature you choose not to.
- **Cocytus.** The cold doesn't take you. You have Resistance to Cold damage, and Advantage on saving throws against the spells and effects of Fiends.
- **The Seven Gates.** No door surprises you. You know where a portal leads before you step through it, and you have Advantage on saving throws against being teleported or moved to another plane against your will.

> **What the Walk Costs**
>
> Walking a plane means facing what it does to visitors, and the DM decides what that was. The planes chapter of the Dungeon Master's Guide is the model, each plane bringing the dangers that belong to its place on the Wheel: the winds of Pandemonium that wear at the mind, Tartarus that holds what it takes, the gray of Asphodel that drains the will to leave, Gehenna's grudging fire, Acheron's endless war, the cruelty of the Nine Circles and the corruption of the Abyss; and on the brighter roads, the joy of Elysium and Svarga's revel that make visitors forget to go home, Eden's garden, where every beast still answers to the name it was given, and Limbo, which takes the shape a mind gives it. A plane isn't walked by a Revelator who was teleported in and out between breaths. The marks aren't worth the trip on their own, and they aren't meant to be: a Revelator who goes to Gehenna for the mark should get the whole of Gehenna.

features.name: Wider Vistas
features.text: When you let in an Influence, you can choose a second creature (it can be you) you can see within 30 feet of the vista. The Influence affects both creatures.

features.name: The Circuit
features.text:
*You understand the shape of the world.*

You learn one Revelation of your choice from the Cosmography's Near Planes, Circuit at Level 7, Borderlands, or Dominions. It can be a plane another pathway grants at level 7. The planes the pathways reach at level 15 are beyond you until The Circuit Made Whole. Before The Circuit Made Whole, The Circuit is the only way to learn:

- **The Borderlands:** the planes in the shadow of the Dominions: Arcadia and the House of Song on either side of the Seven Heavens, Gehenna beside the Nine Circles, Pandemonium beside the Abyss. The roads pass through them (the Styx rises in Pandemonium and runs past Gehenna, and the Path of Judgment crosses Arcadia on its way down from the House of Song), but no pathway stops there. By now you know the roads through them anyway.
- **The Dominions' Quiet Corners:** the Sphere of the Moon, Cocytus, and the Seven Gates.

features.name: Ethereal Wayfarer
features.text:
*The body starts to learn the lessons of the soul.*

**Long Stride.** Ethereal Stride can last up to 1 minute instead of until the end of your turn (as if you were concentrating on a spell), and you can end it as a Bonus Action. Creatures you guide stay in the Border Ethereal with you for the duration, and any of them can return to the Material Plane as a Bonus Action.

**Etherealness.** You can cast *Etherealness* without expending a spell slot. When you do, you can bring a number of willing creatures within 10 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Body Follows
features.text:
*The last aspect of your material form joins you.*

You can cast *Plane Shift* without expending a spell slot or Material components. It can take you only to the Material Plane or to a plane whose Revelation you know, and you arrive exactly where you intend. You can't use this casting to send an unwilling creature to another plane. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Ethereal Sight
features.text:
*Your senses expand with your new perspective.*

Your Veilsight extends to 120 feet, and you and your spirits can see Invisible creatures and objects within that range.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

features.name: The Circuit Made Whole
features.text:
*You understand why the world is the shape that it is.*

You gain the following benefits.

**Every Revelation.** You know every Revelation in the Cosmography. You can call on any plane's Favor, but on no more than nine different planes between rests. Your earth end still grants its Favor twice, and Arete, if you have it, still works.

**Old Acquaintance.** You can use Reach Beyond twice per Long Rest.

**Favor in the Moment.** When you roll Initiative, you regain up to two Favors.

**Spirit of Totality.** When you call a spirit, you can call the Spirit of Totality instead: a spirit of no one plane, sent by all of them together. It is still your one spirit (with The Fare, it counts as both of your spirits), and it uses the Visiting Spirit stat block. It counts as every creature type, and it understands and speaks every language, but it has no Aspect's traits. When you command it, it uses the commands of two different Spirit Aspects of your choice; a command that needs a trait it lacks (such as an element or its light) can't be chosen. While it's with you, each time you hit with your Planar Strike you can choose its damage type from any plane's.

**Walked Whole.** The hard roads add up. For every two hard roads you have walked, Favor in the Moment regains one more Favor. If you have walked all seven, you also have Advantage on the Constitution saving throw for the Strain of Reach Beyond.

subclasses.name: The Path of Judgment
subclasses.lead:
*Endure What You Are Commanded to Endure*

A long stretch of paved road, better kept in some places than others. It comes down from the House of Song's workshops, through Arcadia's orchards and the gears of the Celestial Bureaucracy, and ends at a bridge over the Styx in Acheron. On the far bank, the road becomes the field. Every other road wanders; this one runs straight. Revelators of the Path of Judgment know the road is the first act of resistance to chaos, and they tramp it down.

features.name: Path of Judgment Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Path of Judgment Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Compelled Duel* |
| 5 | *Zone of Truth* |
| 9 | *Slow* |
| 13 | *Stoneskin* |
| 17 | *Geas* |

features.name: The Bridgehead
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Bridgehead, the near end of the last bridge.

features.name: The Scale
features.text:
Whenever you open a vista, of any plane and for any purpose, you can also Weigh one creature you can see within 30 feet of the vista that isn't your ally. It stays Weighed for 1 minute, and only one creature can be Weighed at a time. Weighing a creature again starts its Weighing over.

Each time a Weighed creature deals damage to you or one of your allies, the scale tips (an attack or effect that damages several of you at once tips it only once), and the creature takes 1d6 Force damage. The first time the scale tips, the creature's Speed also decreases by 10 feet until the Weighing ends. If you have at least 1 Hit Point and the damage that tipped the scale was dealt to you by the Weighed creature (including damage you take for an ally through Bear the Verdict), you regain Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier, no more than once between the start of one of your turns and the start of your next. You always know the direction to a Weighed creature on the same plane as you, and it gains no benefit from the Invisible condition against you or your spirits.

**Weighed Together.** From Revelator level 5, the scale also restores you when the damage that tipped it was dealt to an ally: you regain Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier, under the same limit of once between the start of one of your turns and the start of your next.

features.name: Bear the Verdict
features.text: You gain training with Heavy armor, and you have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid being moved or knocked Prone. When an ally within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction, after the damage is rolled, to take the damage instead (any other effect still applies to the ally). If the damage came from a Weighed creature, the scale still tips.

features.name: The Celestial Bureaucracy
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Celestial Bureaucracy.

features.name: The Paperwork
features.text: You can read the seals, stamps, and forms of any office, court, or bureaucracy, in any language: you know whether a document is genuine, what office issued it, and what it lets its bearer do. After an hour in a government office, a customs house, or a court's antechamber, you know whom to see, in what order, and what each of them will want.

features.name: Lockstep
features.text: Your spirit stands where you can't. You can use Bear the Verdict when an ally within 5 feet of your spirit takes damage, as if you were in the spirit's space. You take the damage, not the spirit.

features.name: A Heavier Scale
features.text: The scale's weight shifts onto the Weighed. Each time it tips, the creature also has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn (tips don't stack: one Disadvantage at a time).

features.name: Acheron
features.text: You know the Revelation of Acheron. You've crossed.

features.name: Endure the Sentence
features.text: When you take damage through Bear the Verdict, you have Resistance to it.

features.name: Found Wanting
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you pronounce judgment on a Weighed creature whose scale has tipped at least three times during this Weighing. It makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 6d10 Force damage, loses Concentration, and is banished to an empty stretch of the road until the end of its next turn. It then returns to the space it left (or the nearest unoccupied one), having forgotten the last minute: it still knows its enemies, but not where any creature it can't see is. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Oceanus Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Oceanus Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Bless* |
| 5 | *Aid* |
| 9 | *Mass Healing Word* |
| 13 | *Control Water* |
| 17 | *Mass Cure Wounds* |

features.name: Wellsprings
features.text:
*You hold a vista to the Oceanus open, allowing its waters to flow through.* As a Bonus Action, you can call on the Maelstrom's Favor to open a Wellspring, a vista that fills a 5-foot Cube within 30 feet of yourself. It lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition, and it doesn't require Concentration. You can have only one Wellspring at a time; opening another closes the first. A Wellspring isn't your open vista: opening one doesn't close the vista you have open or replace it, and opening another vista doesn't close a Wellspring.

During combat, whenever you or a creature you can see enters the Wellspring's space for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, you can have that creature regain 1d4 Hit Points (no action required) if it is Bloodied. A Wellspring doesn't heal outside combat. A Wellspring can heal three times, and then it closes. As a Bonus Action, you can move the Wellspring up to 30 feet to a space you can see. You can move it into a creature's space; that counts as the creature entering it. Opening or moving a Wellspring doesn't command your spirit.

features.name: The Maelstrom
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Maelstrom.

features.name: Water-Taken
features.text: You can breathe water. You always know whether water you can see is safe to drink, and if it's fouled (poison, disease, a corpse upstream), which way the fouling came from. The spirits of springs, pools, wells, and rivers know you as one of the water's own, and with your Veilsight they'll talk to you about what they've seen.

features.name: Elysium
features.text: You know the Revelation of Elysium.

features.name: Steady Flow
features.text: A Wellspring heals 1d6 instead of 1d4.

features.name: Clean Water
features.text: Once per Long Rest, you can spend 10 minutes at a well, spring, cistern, or stretch of stream and open the Oceanus into it. All the water within 30 feet of you is cleansed of poison and disease, and water drawn from it stays clean for 24 hours.

features.name: Confluence
features.text: You can have two Wellsprings at once, and a creature that regains Hit Points from one can also end the Poisoned condition on itself.

features.name: What the Water Took
features.text: Once per Long Rest, you can put your hand in a body of water and name a creature or object lost in it within the last year. You learn where it lies, or where it came ashore. If it was a person, you also learn whether they drowned, were taken, or walked out on their own feet, and if they were taken, by what.

features.name: Eden
features.text: You know the Revelation of Eden.

features.name: Cascade
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can pour a Wellspring into one creature within 5 feet of it. The Wellspring closes, and the creature regains 2d6 Hit Points for each time the Wellspring could still have healed.

features.name: The Far Shore
features.text: When a creature dies within sight of you or of one of your Wellsprings, you can tell it the way across (no action required). Its spirit goes on: it doesn't linger as a ghost, and it can't be raised as Undead against its will. This doesn't prevent a spell that returns it to life.

features.name: No True End
features.text: When an ally within 30 feet of one of your Wellsprings drops to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to have it drop to 1 Hit Point instead. It then regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Wisdom modifier. A creature can benefit from this only once per Long Rest.

features.name: Olympus Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Olympus Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Guiding Bolt* |
| 5 | *Enhance Ability* |
| 9 | *Haste* |
| 13 | *Fabricate* |
| 17 | *Legend Lore* |

features.name: The Foot of the Mountain
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Foot of the Mountain.

features.name: Arete
features.text: Between rests, one plane you have already called on can grant its Favor once more, or two planes once you reach Revelator level 11. You can replace a Revelation you chose when you finish a Short Rest, not only a Long Rest.

features.name: Everything Is Next Door
features.text: You gain proficiency with one tool of your choice and learn one language of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can exchange the tool, the language, or both for others: the Mountain lends; it doesn't give.

features.name: Hundred Hands
features.text: When a creature you can see attacks an ally within 5 feet of your spirit, you can take a Reaction to give the attack roll Disadvantage. Your spirit catches the blow, but it takes nothing for it.

features.name: Many-Turning
features.text: When you open a vista to let in an Influence, your spirit can take on that Revelation's Spirit Aspect, including its creature type, instead of its own, without calling on another Favor. Its current Hit Points and Hit Point maximum don't change, and it changes its Aspect only once per vista.

features.name: The Middle World
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Middle World.

features.name: High Places
features.text: When you spend 10 minutes at the top of a hill, tower, mast, or other high place with a wide view, you see the lay of the land for a day's travel around: the roads and rivers, the settlements and their smoke, and anything that's wrong in it (a burned farm, an army's dust, a place where the Veil has worn thin). The DM describes what's there to be seen. You can do this once per Long Rest.

features.name: Twofold Vista
features.text: When you open a vista to let in an Influence, you can let in a second Influence from a different Revelation you know, without calling on its Favor (even if that Favor is spent), on the same creature or another within 30 feet of the vista. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Guest-Friendship
features.text: You always know the customs of hospitality where you are: what to bring, what to refuse, where to sit, and what not to say. You never give offense by accident. While you're someone's guest and have eaten under their roof, you have Advantage on Charisma checks to persuade them.

features.name: Excellence
features.text: Healing and Temporary Hit Points from your Influences increase by your Proficiency Bonus, and an Influence that lasts until the start of your next turn lasts until the end of your next turn instead.

features.name: Svarga
features.text: You know the Revelation of Svarga, the mountain's summit.

features.name: Seen from the Summit
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when you spend an hour studying a person, a place, or an institution (a court, a guild, a city's government, a family), the DM tells you three true things about how it works: who holds it up, what it fears, and what it wants.

features.name: Apotheosis
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you regain a number of Favors equal to half the number in your Revelations column (round up), and for 1 minute you have Advantage on attack rolls for your Planar Strikes. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: The Styx
subclasses.lead:
*Carry Whoever Pays the Fare*

In myth the Styx is the river under the world, circling the land of the dead; on the Wheel it rises in Pandemonium's howling caverns and runs down through the Lower Planes. Revelators of the Styx ferry souls across its placid surface to aid them.

features.name: Styx Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Styx Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Bane* |
| 5 | *Blindness/Deafness* |
| 9 | *Feign Death* |
| 13 | *Confusion* |
| 17 | *Modify Memory* |

features.name: The River Below
features.text: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet, or your Darkvision's range increases by 30 feet if you already have it. You can't become lost underground, and you always know the direction to the nearest water that flows beneath the ground.

features.name: The Fare
features.text: When you call a spirit, you can keep the spirit you already have instead of dismissing it, letting you have two Visiting Spirits at once. When you command your spirits, only one of them uses its Aspect; the other takes its turn as usual. If you call a spirit while you have two, you choose which one leaves.

features.name: Blood in the Pit
features.text: *Your spirits remember the taste of blood.* Once per turn, when you hit a creature with Planar Strike, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice. Roll it, and add the number rolled to the damage.

features.name: The Source Mists
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Source Mists.

features.name: Asphodel
features.text: You know the Revelation of Asphodel.

features.name: Last Rites
features.text: When you see a corpse, you know how long ago it died, and whether its spirit has gone on, lingers nearby, or is being kept from going. You know the funeral customs of any people whose dead you have seen buried, and the dead of those peoples take you seriously: you have Advantage on Charisma checks with spirits of the dead.

features.name: The Unpaid
features.text: When you open a vista, you can let in the Unpaid instead of calling a spirit or letting in an Influence: the shades who couldn't afford the fare. They fill a 15-foot-radius area centered on the vista for 1 minute. The area is Difficult Terrain for your enemies, and an enemy that starts its turn there must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 2d6 Psychic damage (3d6 from Revelator level 11, 4d6 from level 15) and have Disadvantage on its next attack roll. The Unpaid stay for the full minute even if the vista closes. Letting them in doesn't dismiss your spirits, and they don't count against your limit of spirits, but only one crowd of the Unpaid can be in the world at a time.

features.name: Full Passage
features.text: When you command your spirits, both can use their Aspects. When you use Blood in the Pit, you can expend two Hit Point Dice instead of one.

features.name: Tartarus
features.text: You know the Revelation of Tartarus.

features.name: The Ferryman
features.text: The Ferryman's skiff slides out of the mist. As a Bonus Action, you call the Ferryman for 1 minute. At the end of each of your turns while he's present, he can carry up to three willing creatures within 30 feet of you, teleporting each to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The Charmed and Frightened conditions end on any creature he carries; it forgets what charmed or frightened it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Yggdrasil
subclasses.lead:
*Fight With the Dead at Your Back*

The World Ash rises from the wells of Asphodel, and its branches reach through Valhalla, Limbo, and Eden. Revelators of Yggdrasil leap into the gleeful fray with the warrior souls they summon urging them on.

features.name: Yggdrasil Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Yggdrasil Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Heroism* |
| 5 | *Magic Weapon* |
| 9 | *Crusader's Mantle* |
| 13 | *Grasping Vine* |
| 17 | *Tree Stride* |

features.name: Tyr's Hand
features.text: *The bravest of the Aesir has one hand, and he put the other where it went on purpose.* You gain proficiency with Martial weapons. In addition, when a creature within your reach hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can take a Reaction to make one weapon attack against that creature. When you attack with a Light weapon and make the extra attack its Light property allows, you can make that extra attack without spending your Bonus Action, once on each of your turns.

features.name: The Wells
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Wells.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. On a turn when you make your Planar Strike, you can't also make the extra attack of the Light property or the Nick mastery.

features.name: Valhalla
features.text: You know the Revelation of Valhalla.

features.name: The Mead-Bench
features.text: Soldiers, mercenaries, sailors, and any other company that drinks together before a fight take you for one of their own after an evening in their company. They'll share their rumors, their billets, and their grievances with you, and in any town with a garrison or a harbor, you can find a bed among them for the night at no cost.

features.name: Rise Each Dawn
features.text: When you drop to 0 Hit Points and don't die outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Falcon Cloak
features.text: *Freyja's feather-cloak is lent to you, as it was to Loki.* When you command your spirit, you can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. While you're within 5 feet of your spirit, creatures can't make Opportunity Attacks against you.

features.name: Limbo
features.text: You know the Revelation of Limbo.

features.name: Rise Together
features.text: Rise Each Dawn recharges when you finish a Short or Long Rest. When an ally you can see within 30 feet of yourself drops to 0 Hit Points and doesn't die outright, you can take a Reaction to spend Rise Each Dawn on that ally instead: it drops to 1 Hit Point.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Revelator's skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields
multiclass.text: You must have a Wisdom score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Revelator Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Revelator's skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields. Gain the Revelator's level 1 features, which are listed in the Revelator Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Revelator levels (round up), as you would Ranger levels. Your Revelations and your Planar Strike dice come only from your Revelator levels. If you have levels in another class and fewer than five Revelator levels, you can call a spirit with Visiting Spirit only once, and you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

data.name: Danae
data.blurb: Cha full caster. The fae, and the Hidden’s courts.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Nature, Persuasion, Religion, or Sleight of Hand

*Choose 2:* Calligrapher's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Gaming Set, Glassblower's Tools, Herbalism Kit, Jeweler's Tools, Mason's Tools, Musical Instrument, Navigator's Tools, Painter's Supplies, Weaver's Tools, or Woodcarver's Tools
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, 2 Daggers, Quarterstaff, Arcane Focus (crystal), Explorer's Pack, and 16 GP; or (B) 50 GP.

rows.Class Features: The Elder Cycles, The Door Opens

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
Danae learn their spells through dream. Each night, the Hidden communicates with them deep in their unconscious, and when they awake, they know what magic to prepare.

**Cantrips.** You know three cantrips of your choice from the Danae spell list. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Danae spell list. When you reach Danae levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Danae spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Danae Features table.

**Spell Slots.** The Danae Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Danae spell list. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Danae levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Danae Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Danae spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Danae feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Danae spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Danae spells for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Danae spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus, or any tool from the Danae's tool list or your subclass's tool that you have proficiency with, as a Spellcasting Focus for your Danae spells: the work of your hands is where the Wyrd, the Hidden's weaving of what comes to pass, comes through.

features.name: The Sight
features.text: You see the Hidden's layer over the world. You can see thresholds between worlds within 30 feet of yourself (a threshold is a fixed place where the settled world touches another realm, such as the Hidden; the DM decides where they lie), and you know when a creature or an object you can see is under an illusion or a shape-changing effect, or has the Fey creature type, and whether it is a Hidden creature. You also gain proficiency in the Insight and Perception skills (if you already have proficiency in either, choose another skill from the Danae's skill list), and you know Sylvan, the Hidden's own speech.

features.name: Warps
features.text:
Once you see the true shape of reality, you gain the ability to manipulate its space.

As a Bonus Action, you warp an unoccupied 5-foot Cube you can see within 60 feet of yourself into one of the shapes below. The warp lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you unravel it. You can make a number of warps equal to the number in the Warps column of the Danae Features table, and you regain all expended warps when you finish a Short or Long Rest. A warp that is still in place when you finish the rest (a readied lot, say, or a stave) stays expended until it ends; a warp that ends when you finish the rest is regained with the others. Warps don't require Concentration, and they don't choose sides: a warp affects every creature alike, unless its season says otherwise. Warps can't overlap: no part of a warp's space can be part of another warp's space. A warp is a visible thing: a creature that can see its space can tell that the space is wrong, though not what the warp does until it's inside. When a warp calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

- **Stretch.** Every foot of movement inside the warp costs 2 extra feet. This doesn't stack with Difficult Terrain: inside a Stretch, each foot costs 3 feet either way.
- **Gate.** Your Gates are linked in a chain, in the order you made them; the last leads back to the first. A Gate must rest on a surface. A creature that enters a Gate steps out of the next one in the chain, in its space or the nearest unoccupied space to it. This costs no movement and doesn't trigger the Gate it arrives in. A creature can pass through your Gates only once per turn. If a Gate ends, the chain closes around the gap: the Gate before it leads to the Gate after it. A lone Gate leads nowhere.

**Unraveling.** Some features let you unravel a warp. To unravel a warp, you either end one of your warps that is in place or expend one you haven't used yet; either way, the feature takes effect. A feature that tells you to expend a warp uses one you haven't used yet.

**Magic and Travel.** Warps are magical effects: *Detect Magic* reveals them, and *Dispel Magic* ends one as if it were a level 1 spell. Passing through a Gate, or any warp that takes a creature from one space to another without crossing the space between, is teleportation; a push or a fall is not.

**Arriving by Teleport.** A creature teleported into a warp's space enters the warp, just as if it had walked in, but a Gate it arrives in doesn't send it on. A creature can't arrive inside a stone's solid space; it arrives in the nearest unoccupied space instead. If nothing in that space would hold a creature standing (the warp hangs in the air or over a drop), the creature instead arrives in the nearest unoccupied space where it can stand, and it doesn't enter the warp. A creature passing through a pair of Doors (a Crossing Danae's warp; see Crossing) follows the Doors' own rules instead.

features.name: The Half
features.text:
You gravitate, in one fashion or another, to one half of the Hidden's year. Choose the light half or the dark half. The light half's seasons are spring and summer; the dark half's, autumn and winter.

**Seasons.** You learn your half's two seasons. When you make a warp, you can give it one season you know. A creature that enters a seasoned warp for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, is subject to its season, making any saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature is subject to the season of only one of your warps per turn: the first that takes it.

| Half | Season | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Light | **Spring** | *Strength saving throw.* On a failed save, you move the creature up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice. A willing creature can instead teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. |
| Light | **Summer** | The creature takes 1d6 Fire damage. Creatures you choose when you make the warp are immune. The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach Danae levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6). |
| Dark | **Autumn** | *Wisdom saving throw.* On a failed save, choose one: the creature has the Charmed condition, with you as the charmer, until the start of its next turn, or it has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn. |
| Dark | **Winter** | *Constitution saving throw.* On a failed save, the creature's Speed is 0 and it can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. A creature that fails this save can't be affected by the same warp's winter again. |

features.name: Denial
features.text:
You refuse the outcome others would have for you, and change things accordingly.

When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor or using a Shield, you can take a Reaction and unravel one of your warps to deny it. You gain a bonus to AC equal to the Proficiency Bonus for your Danae level (as shown in the Danae Features table), to a maximum of +5, until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering attack.

How reality rearranges itself follows your nature, and from level 3 your subclass:

| | The blow is denied by |
|---|---|
| Before level 3 | a flicker of the Hidden: a scent of rain, a wrong-colored light, and the blow goes wide |
| Binding | a thread that catches the weapon an inch short |
| Changing | a hidden current pulling at them |
| Crossing | the air folding, and the blow arriving somewhere you aren't |
| Naming | a word: the blow is named a miss |
| Shaping | stone or crystal rising across the skin |

features.name: Flee
features.text:
When you take damage and are Bloodied afterward but not at 0 Hit Points (whether or not you were Bloodied before), you can take a Reaction to step half out of the world. Unravel one or more of your warps, in place (lots, knots, and staves included) or not yet used; each warp unraveled is 1 **fuel**. You're **Away** for 1 minute, and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Danae level, plus 5 for each fuel. These Temporary Hit Points replace any you already have.

Being Away ends early when you have none of its Temporary Hit Points left, when you have the Incapacitated condition, or when you end it (no action required). While you're Away, you keep your mind and your magic: you cast spells and keep Concentration as normal, and in addition:

- **Half Here.** Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.
- **Flicker.** Once on each of your turns, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see (no action required).

**Readjust.** When you stop being Away, you come back not quite where or when you left: you reappear in an unoccupied space within 15 feet of where you were, chosen by the DM (or by you, if the DM doesn't choose), and you can't take Reactions until the end of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Danae Subclass
features.text: Your prime modality manifests: you gain a Danae subclass of your choice: Binding, Changing, Crossing, Naming, or Shaping. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Danae levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Danae level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Danae levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Fae Weaving
features.text:
The Wyrd flows through your hands, granting you what you might need in a given moment.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can weave fae material into the world with a tool you have proficiency with from the Danae's tool list or your subclass's tool. You create up to a number of nonmagical objects equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Each must be something that tool could make, Medium or smaller, not a consumable (food, a potion, an oil, a poison, or the like) and not ammunition, and worth no more than 10 GP × your Danae level. A tool that makes nothing under the crafting rules weaves the small things of its trade: a Gaming Set dice, cards, and boards; a Musical Instrument strings, reeds, and pipes; Thieves' Tools picks, keys, and wires. The objects are real and work as the real thing, but anyone who handles one feels that it is strange. They come undone when you next finish a Long Rest or when you use this feature again.

**Fairy Gold.** The objects are fairy gold: any of them turns to dross when it changes hands for value, and none can be used as a Material component that has a cost.

features.name: The First Cycles
features.text:
Your warps can be 5-foot or 10-foot Cubes, and you learn two more shapes:

- **Tilt.** You choose which way is down within the warp. A creature that enters it or starts its turn there must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall that way until it hits a surface or leaves the warp. This is a normal fall: the creature takes damage for the distance it fell and, if it takes any, has the Prone condition. It can then walk on the surface it fell to. When the warp ends, down is down again, and a creature left in the air falls.
- **Pocket.** The warp is bigger inside than out. A creature enters it by moving into its space, and a creature inside can leave by spending 5 feet of movement to appear in an unoccupied space next to it. Up to eight Medium creatures fit inside it, whatever its size (a Small or Tiny creature counts as one, a Large creature as four, and a Huge or larger creature can't enter; nor can a creature that wouldn't fit beside those already inside), and anything inside has Total Cover against anything outside, and the reverse. When a Pocket ends, each creature inside it appears in the nearest unoccupied space.

features.name: Reading the Season
features.text:
The Hidden settles in you, and you begin to read people as it reads them, by their weather. As a Bonus Action, or as part of rolling Initiative, choose a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself, up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). The DM tells you each one's temper and what lies under it (see Tempers, below). For 1 hour, you have Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against each of them, and on Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion) checks against them that play to their tempers.

**Tempers.** Every creature has a temper, which is always one of the four seasons. The DM assigns it from the creature's mood at the moment: spring (hope, curiosity, a beginning), summer (passion, anger, confidence), autumn (longing, regret, decline), or winter (fear, grief, resolve). If the DM is unsure, roll a d4: 1 spring, 2 summer, 3 autumn, 4 winter. A temper holds until the creature's mood plainly changes or the scene ends. A feature that turns a temper (Name the Season, the Hidden Bard's Turn the Season) sets it for that feature's duration instead. A player character's temper is the player's to say when it's read; if the player doesn't, the DM assigns it. A feature that turns a player character's temper changes its season for this book's features only: its attitude doesn't shift, and how the character feels is still the player's to play. Every feature in this book that uses tempers follows this rule.

features.name: Open Book
features.text: You can cast *Detect Thoughts* without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. A creature whose temper you've read with Reading the Season in the last hour has Disadvantage on its saving throw against the spell.

features.name: The Way Back
features.text:
You regain the use of Flee when you finish a Short or Long Rest, and when you Readjust, you always choose the space where you reappear.

In addition, while you're Away, when you teleport with Flicker, you can leave a warp of any shape you know in the space you left. It follows every rule for your warps (it can't overlap another, it lasts 1 minute, it can carry a season you know, and it counts as one of your warps in place), except that it costs no Bonus Action and no warp.

features.name: Thresholds
features.text: Your Sight expands, allowing you to see paths into the Hidden itself. You can spend 1 minute at a threshold you can see with The Sight to open it, casting *Plane Shift* without expending a spell slot or needing its Material component. The spell targets you and up to eight willing creatures, it can take you only to or from the Hidden, and you arrive at the threshold's other side. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Loop
features.text:
You learn another warp shape:

- **Loop.** The warp's edges meet. When a creature tries to leave the warp by any means, moving or teleporting, or is moved out of it against its will, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it steps back in from the opposite side. The movement it spent leaving is lost (as is any spell slot or use the teleport cost), and it can't try to leave that Loop again until its next turn. A creature that succeeds can't be held by that Loop again for 1 minute.

features.name: The Middle Cycles
features.text: You learn the other half's two seasons. A warp still holds only one season.

features.name: Name the Season
features.text: As a Magic action, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself whose temper you've read with Reading the Season in the last hour. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you turn its temper to another season of your choice for 1 hour; its mood follows, its attitude toward you shifts one step (Hostile to Indifferent, or Indifferent to Friendly, or the reverse), and it doesn't know it was touched. On a successful save, it knows something tried. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Hill
features.text:
You learn another warp shape:

- **Hill.** Time inside the warp runs at the hill's pace. A creature that starts its turn inside the warp must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or, until the start of its next turn, its Speed is halved, it can't take Reactions, and on its turn it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both. When a creature leaves a Hill after failing a save against it, it doesn't remember what happened while it was inside.

features.name: Blasé
features.text: The Hidden doesn't let its own be led. You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

features.name: The Elder Cycles
features.text: You can call the whole year at once. As a Bonus Action, choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Every creature of your choice in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered there is subject to all four seasons, making each saving throw separately. A season's effect that would last until the start of a creature's next turn lasts until the end of its next turn instead. To resolve it quickly, each creature rolls its Constitution and Wisdom saving throws together, then its Strength saving throw (summer's damage needs no saving throw). Move the creatures that failed against spring last. This isn't a warp's season: it doesn't count against the one-warp-a-turn limit, and a creature can still be subject to one of your warps' seasons on the same turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Door Opens
features.text:
While you're Away, the door you carry stands open, and you gain these benefits:

- **The Storm.** At the start of each of your turns, each creature of your choice in a 15-foot Emanation originating from you is subject to a season. A creature whose temper you've read with Reading the Season in the last hour is subject to the season of its temper, and it has Disadvantage on any saving throw against it; every other creature is subject to one season you know, chosen when the storm starts each turn. This counts as one of your warps' seasons, so a creature it takes can't be taken by a warp's season on the same turn. A season's effect that would last until the start of a creature's next turn lasts until the end of its next turn instead.
- **The Glamour Drops.** Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 30 feet of you, can see you, and whose temper you've read with Reading the Season in the last hour makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has your choice of the Frightened or Charmed condition, with you as the source, until the start of its next turn.

features.name: Second Sight
features.text: The Sight opens all the way. You have Truesight with a range of 60 feet. When you use Reading the Season, you can read any number of creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: Twist of Fate
features.text:
When you roll Initiative, you regain up to two expended warps, and you can then make up to two warps (no action required). Each warp you make this way expends a warp, as usual.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to turn the moment: it succeeds instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Binding
subclasses.lead: You learn the arts of binding yourself and others, whether with word, thread, or root.

features.name: Binding Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Binding Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Dissonant Whispers*, *Hex*, *Warding Bond*, *Zone of Truth* |
| 5 | *Bestow Curse*, *Magic Circle* |
| 7 | *Compulsion*, *Phantasmal Killer* |
| 9 | *Dream*, *Planar Binding* |

features.name: Courtly Grace
features.text: You carry yourself as the most elevated of fae nobles. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. You have Advantage on Charisma checks you make against a creature that is knotted by you.

features.name: Knots
features.text:
Your warps can be knots. As a Bonus Action, you tie a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to another creature or to a fixed point within 30 feet of it (the ground, a tree, a door), and speak a geis into the knot. Each unwilling creature you tie makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; if any succeeds, no knot is tied, though the warp is still expended. A geis binds each unwilling creature in the knot; a willing creature is tied but not bound. An unwilling knotted creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, and the knot comes undone on a success. While knotted, it has Disadvantage on saving throws against your seasons. Choose the geis:

- **Stay.** It can't willingly move more than 30 feet from what it's tied to.
- **Spare.** It can't willingly target what it's tied to with an attack or a harmful effect.
- **Heed.** It has Disadvantage on attack rolls against anything but what it's tied to. When it attacks something else, it can break the geis instead of taking the Disadvantage.

*Breaking a Geis.* A knotted creature can choose to break its geis when it is about to do what the geis forbids: to walk away, to strike, to turn. If it does, it first takes Psychic damage equal to 2d8 plus your Charisma modifier, and the knot comes undone; then, if it can still act, it does what it chose. The damage increases to 3d8 at Danae level 10 and 4d8 at level 14.

features.name: Kind Words
features.text:
Your words echo with the terrible grace of the Fair.

As a Bonus Action, choose a creature that is knotted by you and that can hear and understand you, and speak to it. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has your choice of the Frightened or Charmed condition, with you as the source, until the end of its next turn. At the start of any of its turns, the creature can defy you (no action required): it takes the same Psychic damage as breaking a geis, and then the condition ends.

You can win the same argument only once: a creature affected by your Kind Words can't be affected by them again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Heartstrings
features.text: Creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against your Kind Words. When your Kind Words succeed against a creature knotted to another creature, you can choose to have the other affected too, without a saving throw; it counts as affected by your Kind Words.

features.name: Handfast
features.text: Outside combat, you can spend 10 minutes tying a binding between two or more willing creatures who make a promise to each other in your presence: a marriage, a contract, an apprenticeship, a truce, a sworn friendship. This costs no warp and isn't a knot for your other features. While the binding holds, each creature in it knows when another breaks the promise, and knows roughly which direction the others lie in, at any distance on the same plane. The binding holds until every creature in it agrees to untie it, or until you untie it. You can keep a number of bindings equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); tying another unties your oldest.

features.name: Oath
features.text: As a Magic action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that is knotted by you or that your Kind Words have affected within the last minute, and name a promise: to yield, to flee, to stand aside, to tell the truth, or not to harm a creature you name. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, the promise binds it for 1 hour. The first time it breaks the promise, it takes 6d10 Psychic damage, and you know. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Thrall
features.text: As a Magic action, you take hold of a creature knotted by you that you can see. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, with Disadvantage if it has the Charmed or Frightened condition from you. On a failed save, it is under your control until the end of your next turn, as the *Dominate Monster* spell, but the effect doesn't require Concentration. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Changing Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Changing Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Augury*, *Bane*, *Bless*, *Enhance Ability* |
| 5 | *Beacon of Hope*, *Clairvoyance* |
| 7 | *Death Ward*, *Divination* |
| 9 | *Commune*, *Contact Other Plane* |

features.name: Lots
features.text:
Your warps can be lots. As a Bonus Action, you ready one: you roll the coin across your knuckles, shake the die, palm the card. A readied lot counts as a warp, and it lasts until you cast it or finish a Long Rest.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to cast a readied lot after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether it succeeds, and call it:

- **Fair.** The creature rolls another d20 and uses the higher roll.
- **Foul.** The creature rolls another d20 and uses the lower roll.

A lot you cast is spent.

features.name: Flow of Fate
features.text: The stream of fate runs under everyone near you, and you can pull it aside for them as easily as for yourself. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is hit by an attack roll, you can use Denial for it instead of for yourself, unraveling one of your readied lots; the creature gains the bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering attack. Denial's armor restriction applies to you, not to the creature you protect.

features.name: Small Mercies
features.text: Outside combat, when you or a companion goes looking for something ordinary you need (a dropped key, a cheap item a market might stock, a carter going your way, someone who knows the pass), the DM tells you where it turns up, if it can be found anywhere nearby. You can also tell when a game, a lottery, a drawing of lots, or a wager is rigged (marked cards, loaded dice, a fixed draw) by watching one round of it; you don't learn how, only that the house is cheating fate. Once you find something this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Losing Streak
features.text: When you call foul and the creature fails the check or saving throw or misses with the attack roll, you regain one expended warp. Once you regain a warp this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Road Luck
features.text: While you travel overland or by water with companions, the road's small mishaps don't befall your company unless the DM wants one for the story: no thrown shoe, cracked axle, spoiled flour, or missed tide. Further, when your company's way is uncertain (a fork, a fog, two inns), you can ask the DM which choice the year favors, and the DM answers "this one," "that one," or "neither." Once you ask, you can't ask again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Double or Nothing
features.text: When you ready a lot, you can ready a second as part of the same Bonus Action, expending a warp for each. When you cast a lot on an attack roll and the attack hits, the same call carries to the damage: the attacker rerolls the damage dice and uses the higher total (fair) or the lower (foul).

features.name: Lucky Charm
features.text: Gamblers, sailors, soldiers, midwives, brides, and anyone else who lives by chance can tell what you are after a few minutes in your company. They want you to blow on their dice, touch their nets, and stand at the back of the wedding. You have Advantage on Charisma checks to win over such people, and in any town you can support a Modest lifestyle by being lucky at people, without other work.

features.name: Loaded
features.text: When you cast a lot, instead of calling fair or foul, you can choose the number the roll uses (if the creature rolled more than one d20, the roll uses only the number you choose). The number counts as rolled: a chosen 20 is a natural 20 (a Critical Hit on an attack roll), and a chosen 1 is a natural 1. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Coincidence
features.text: Outside combat, you can let the stream bring you a coincidence. Tell the DM what you need. The DM introduces it in the next scene or soon after, in the form the story allows: the person you were looking for is at the next table, a letter arrives a day early, the ship you missed is still in port because its captain lost at cards. The DM decides the form, and a coincidence never conjures what couldn't plausibly be there. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Crossing
subclasses.lead: Space and barriers are no obstacle to you. You cut your own path as you go.

features.name: Crossing Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Crossing Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Arcane Lock*, *Knock*, *Protection from Evil and Good*, *Silence* |
| 5 | *Gaseous Form*, *Nondetection* |
| 7 | *Freedom of Movement*, *Private Sanctum* |
| 9 | *Steel Wind Strike*, *Teleportation Circle* |

features.name: Doors
features.text:
Your warps can be Doors. As a Bonus Action, you open a pair of linked Doors on solid surfaces you can see within 60 feet of yourself: a wall, a floor, a ceiling, the side of a cart. The pair counts as one warp. Each Door is a 5-foot square, or a 10-foot square from Danae level 5, and a creature fits through it only if the creature's space is no wider than the Door. A creature that moves into one Door steps out of the other, facing away from its surface. When a feature refers to a warp's space, a Door's space is the space in front of it, as wide as the Door and 5 feet deep.

*Inertia.* A creature can pass through the same pair of Doors only once per turn. A creature that falls into a Door comes out of the other still moving. It travels up to the distance it had already fallen, in the direction the far Door faces, before it falls normally or strikes something. When it lands or strikes something, it takes damage as for one fall of the whole distance it fell and traveled, and has the Prone condition if it takes any.

*Back Ways.* After you spend a day in a settlement, you know its back ways: you can find a route between any two places in it that avoids its main streets, watch posts, and toll gates, if such a route exists. After you spend an hour in a building, you know every way into and out of it that a person could use (doors, windows, chimneys, drains, the servants' stair), even the ones its owner has forgotten.

*Keyhole.* One of your Doors can open on a surface you can't see, if it's within 30 feet of yourself and on the far side of a wall, door, floor, or ceiling no more than 5 feet thick. You know whether the space beyond is open before you commit to it.

features.name: Threshold Blade
features.text:
You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill and with Martial weapons that have the Finesse property. When you attack with a Simple weapon or one of these, you can use your Charisma modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

*Through the Warp.* Once on each of your turns, when you make a melee attack with a weapon against a creature within 5 feet of one of your warps within 60 feet of yourself, you can make it from the warp's space. Your blade appears there. For any Reaction the attack triggers, you are in that space. You can't cast a spell as part of that attack or when it hits.

features.name: Seams
features.text: Every warp that fills a space is a Gate for you, whatever its shape: when you enter one of your warps, you can step out of any other. This counts as passing through your Gates, so you can do it only once per turn. While you're in one of your warps, you can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action, and you don't need cover to hide there.

features.name: Unexpected Angle
