features.text: Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack you make from a warp's space with Through the Warp, and the creature can't see you or the warp's space is on the far side of the creature from you (a line from the center of your space to the center of the warp's space passes through the creature's space), the attack deals an extra 2d6 Force damage. The extra damage increases to 3d6 at Danae level 10 and 4d6 at level 14.

features.name: Misplace
features.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack using a weapon, you can unravel one of your warps. The creature makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it is teleported into the space of another of your warps within 60 feet of yourself, or the nearest unoccupied space, and that warp's season, if any, takes it at once.

You can misplace things, too. As a Bonus Action, choose an object within 60 feet of yourself that isn't armor or clothing a creature is wearing or an object a creature is attuned to, and unravel one of your warps. If a creature is holding or carrying it, the creature makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the object appears in your hand or in the space of one of your warps. An object no one is holding or carrying gets no save.

features.name: Liminality
features.text: Your Gates and Doors work through effects that block teleportation or planar travel in a place (a ward, a circle, a hallowed or forbidden area), other than an *Antimagic Field*. An effect that stops a particular creature from teleporting (Cold Iron, Name It, the Iron Bell, a Hidden Killer's ward, a Faebreaker's grip) still stops that creature. Creatures that pass through them don't trigger *Alarm*, *Glyph of Warding*, or similar warding magic, and need no invitation: an effect that keeps out creatures who haven't been invited doesn't stop a creature passing through your Gates and Doors. On foot, you're bound by such effects like anyone else (iron and salt at a door among them).

features.name: Outside
features.text: When an attack roll hits you or you fail a saving throw, you can take a Reaction and unravel one of your warps to step outside reality: the attack or effect does nothing to you. Until the start of your next turn, you can't be seen, targeted, or affected by anything, and you can't affect anything, though you keep Concentration. At the start of your next turn, you step back in, in the space you left or in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Naming
subclasses.lead: You have learned the Names of all things, and you carve them into wood for control and consumption.

features.name: Naming Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Naming Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Arcanist's Magic Aura*, *Identify*, *Illusory Script*, *Locate Object* |
| 5 | *Glyph of Warding*, *Tongues* |
| 7 | *Fire Shield*, *Locate Creature* |
| 9 | *Legend Lore*, *Scrying* |

features.name: Define
features.text:
Your warps can be staves of *feda*. As a Bonus Action, you define a creature, an object, or a place you can see within 60 feet of yourself, cutting its Name into a stave. A stave counts as a warp, but it doesn't end after 1 minute: it lasts until you finish a Long Rest or release it (no action required).

- **Named Creature.** You know its creature type, its Resistances, Immunities, and Vulnerabilities, and which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus. It can't hide from you, and the Invisible condition gives it no benefit against you. It also makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has Disadvantage on saving throws against your warps while the stave lasts. On a successful save, the stave is still cut and you still learn what it tells you, but the creature has no Disadvantage against your warps, and you can't cut its Name again until you finish a Long Rest.
- **Named Object.** You can name only an object you have held, and only one object at a time; naming another releases the first. As a Bonus Action, you can summon it to your hand from anywhere on the same plane, unless another creature is holding or wearing it.
- **Named Place.** You always know the direction and distance to it.

*Ask the Name.* When you cut a Name, you can ask the DM one question about the thing you named, the kind of thing its Name would know: what it really is, who made it or owns it, where it has been, what was done there, what it wants. The DM answers truthfully, in a few words or a single image. You can ask a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can ask about any one creature, object, or place only once per Long Rest. A Named creature that succeeds on its Charisma saving throw keeps its answer to itself.

features.name: Call
features.text: When you cut a Name, you can also make a warp as part of the same Bonus Action, expending a warp for it as usual. In addition, as a Bonus Action, you can speak the Name of a Named creature you can see, expending a warp. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, it is teleported into the space of one of your warps within 60 feet of yourself, or the nearest unoccupied space.

features.name: Rename
features.text:
As a Magic action, you rename a Named creature, object, or place for 1 minute. It doesn't change: the renaming does only what the option you choose says, and nothing else about the thing is different. A creature, or an object a creature is holding or wearing, makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC to resist (the holder makes it for the object). Choose one:

- **Creature: Kind.** Effects that detect creatures by type, or that keep out, admit, or ward against creatures of a type (*Detect Evil and Good*, *Hallow*, *Magic Circle*, *Protection from Evil and Good*, a glyph or ward keyed to a type), treat it as a creature type of your choice. Nothing else does: damage, what a spell can target, and what an effect does once it applies all use its true type.
- **Creature: Size.** Grapples, shoves, and effects that swallow, engulf, carry, or restrain creatures only up to a certain size treat it as one size larger or smaller (your choice). It takes up the space it always has.
- **Object: Purpose.** It is named another kind of object, and it serves only as that. Choose one: *Shut* (a door, gate, lid, or window named a wall can't be opened, short of breaking it); *Open* (a lock named open is unlocked); *Harmless* (a weapon or piece of ammunition named a feather deals no damage); or *Plain* (it looks, feels, and sounds like another nonmagical object of the same size or smaller, a cup named a crown, or a crown a cup, though *Detect Magic*, *Identify*, and The Sight see it as it is). A renamed object never gains magical properties, never counts as a Material component with a cost, and isn't treasure.
- **Place: Threshold.** A space up to a 10-foot Cube is named a threshold to the Hidden, which The Sight can see and Thresholds can open. This renaming lasts 10 minutes instead of 1.
- **Place: Home.** A space up to a 30-foot Cube is named your home. A creature you haven't invited can't willingly enter it.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Lasting Staves
features.text: Your staves last through Long Rests until you release them, though a Named creature's Disadvantage still ends when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Unmake
features.text: As a Magic action, you burn the stave of a Named creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, for 1 minute the world forgets what it is: it loses all its Resistances and Immunities, including Immunities to conditions; effects that rely on its creature type don't apply to it; and it takes 4d10 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns as its Name burns. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful save, it takes 4d10 Fire damage once. The stave is consumed either way. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Shaping
subclasses.lead: You see the true shape of reality and alter it to your whims.

features.name: Shaping Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Shaping Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Floating Disk*, *Ice Knife*, *Levitate*, *Shatter* |
| 5 | *Meld into Stone*, *Tiny Hut* |
| 7 | *Fabricate*, *Stoneskin* |
| 9 | *Animate Objects*, *Creation* |

features.name: Stones
features.text: Your warps can be stones. A stone turns its Cube into solid ground, a wall (Total Cover), or a bridge, or opens a 10-foot-deep pit beneath its space. It is real, not an illusion; it has AC 15 and 30 Hit Points per 5-foot Cube. You can't make a stone that would leave a creature with no unoccupied space it could reach. Anything precious made this way is fairy gold (see Fae Weaving) and can't be made permanent.

features.name: Quick Weaving
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a warp to weave one object as Fae Weaving describes, without waiting for a rest and even before you have that feature. It lasts for 1 minute.

features.name: Deep Ground
features.text:
Your stones gain shapes: a ramp or stair; a pillar that rises under a creature, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be lifted 10 feet (when the stone ends, the pillar sinks back, lowering anything on it to the ground); or the ground opening beneath a creature, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall into a 10-foot-deep pit and have the Prone condition (when the stone ends, the ground rises back, lifting anything in the pit to the surface). A creature that succeeds moves to the nearest unoccupied space beside the stone. Unlike other warps, a pillar or an opening can be made in an occupied space, but only once per turn. Each stone takes only one shape.

With 1 hour of work, you can make a stone permanent; it no longer counts as a warp, so the warp it used comes back when you next finish a Short or Long Rest. You can have a number of permanent stones equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); making another ends your oldest.

features.name: Dream Made Real
features.text: When you cast an illusion spell of level 1 or higher, you can make one object or surface in it real for up to 1 minute. It must be Large or smaller and nonmagical, it can't deal damage, and it can't be made in a creature's space or enclose one. It is solid, bears weight, and blocks movement, and it is fairy gold.

features.name: Quarry
features.text: As a Magic action, you can place up to twelve 10-foot-Cube stones at once within 60 feet of yourself, in any shapes you know, ignoring the once-per-turn limit on pillars and openings. They don't expend warps, and they last 1 hour; with 8 hours of work, the whole shape can be made permanent, and it counts as one of your permanent stones. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Danae Traits table: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor. Gain the Danae's level 1 features, which are listed in the Danae Features table, except The Sight's skill proficiencies. For multiclass spell slots, add all your Danae levels, as you would Wizard levels. If you have levels in another class, you regain expended warps only when you finish a Long Rest.
